docs.title: Michael Burry's top 10 life lessons for GenZ: 'Buy half the house you can afford'
docs.text:
Popular American investor Michael Burry , known for his impeccable ability to spot market bubbles despite frenzy, was asked to give life advice to a 26-year-old GenZ. The 'Big Short' fame market veteran listed 10 pieces of advice in a substack post, including some linked to how one manages personal finance.
 Michael Burry rose to fame after he correctly predicted the 2008 housing crisis. He has recently been ramping up his bets against the AI frenzy, screaming a big crash ahead once the bubble around the new technology bursts. 
Also read | Michael Burry bets against these 4 AI stocks, one of which rallied 190% YTD. Will his AI bubble warnings come true? 
Moving away from his typical bearish predictions, Burry gave some life advice to a 26-year-old in a Substack post on his channel ‘Cassandra Unchained’. Here are the 10 life lessons listed by him.
 Life advice by Michael Burry 
 Live Events
Burry advised the young generation to never stop exercising or learning. He also suggested that people should accept compromise to begin relationships. The popular investor additionally feels people should have kids and be good parents.
It is important to be thankful for and to all, as well as be charitable, according to Burry. "Art in the eye of the beholder is cheap," he wrote. One user commented, asking him if by this he meant people should keep in mind what they value as art doesn't need to be expensive, and they can find joy in things that are free as just because something is expensive doesn’t make it valuable. Burry replied that this is what he meant.
 Michael Burry's personal finance advice 
Michael Burry said people should never gamble and should manifest the power compounding. Notably, legendary investor Warren Buffett and others too have repeatedly advised investors to stay patient and continue to compound. 
The ‘Big Short’ fame investor also spoke about an issue that remains a key doubt for most GenZ - when to buy a house. “Buy half the house you can afford,” he said. Ironically, the market veteran who is advising people to buy house was the one who correctly predicted the housing crisis in the US which triggered a global financial crisis in 2008.
“If it flies or floats, rent it,” Burry said, referring to discretionary spending on depreciating assets like planes and boats. 
Also read | Warren Buffett’s 6 golden rules for investors after retirement 
 Michael Burry’s AI warnings 
Michael Burry has been ramping up his warnings over the excessive optimism about AI. Recently, he said that the market is currently in a 'denial' mood, a phase that could last six to nine months, as seen during the previous 2000 and 2008 crises.
He recently cited data which showed that it would take only a season in which AI revenue disappoints the massive capital expenditure that hyperscalers are putting behind it. “In that scenario, a handful of boards, predisposed to redeploy capital toward the highest-conviction bet, would simply need to conclude that the highest-conviction bet has shifted,” the report said.
This comes after Burry said in August that the AI crash could begin from 2028. However, his latest comments imply that he expects this to happen sooner. Recently, he said the President Donald Trump-led US administration cannot afford to let the AI boom fail. He explained that AI infrastructure buildout has become a critical support for the US economy, keeping very little room for the Trump administration to let the ongoing AI boom weaken, Stockwits reported. Notably, Burry has been shorting AI-linked stocks and warning investors of a sharp selloff ahead.
Also read | AI bubble to burst sooner than expected? Michael Burry believes it would take only one season of revenue disappointment

docs.title: BSE shares jump over 4% as Motilal Oswal upgrades stock to Buy. 4 reasons behind bullish call
docs.text:
Shares of BSE rallied as much as 4.3% to their day’s high of Rs 3,369 on the BSE on Monday after Motilal Oswal upgraded the stock to Buy and assigned a target price of Rs 4,000, an upside of 23%.
 BSE’s scalable business model allows incremental revenue to translate into healthy profit growth. Its EBITDA margin rose sharply to over 65% in FY26 from 9% in FY21, reflecting strong operating leverage, the brokerage said.
With margins projected to expand further to 70%, PAT is expected to grow at a CAGR of around 27% over FY26-28, against a revenue CAGR of 23%. Regulatory costs, which account for 55% of operating expenses and are variable in nature, also offer some protection against a slowdown in trading volumes.
 1.) Strong growth path - Since BSE relaunched derivatives in 2023, the impact of most regulatory changes, including F&O 2.0 and the shift in weekly expiry day, has been temporary. BSE achieved around 50% market share in index options notional turnover within three years of the relaunch, while volumes continued to show strong momentum.
However, recent regulatory changes, including stricter lending norms for proprietary traders effective July 2026 and CAS implementation in August 2026, led to a reset in the volume base. BSE’s notional F&O average daily traded turnover (ADTO) fell 35% in August 2026 compared with the April-July 2026 average.
 Live Events
Following the reset, September 2026 saw a modest recovery, with ADTO rising 6% month-on-month. Volumes picked up significantly in October amid volatile markets, with ADTO up 49% month-on-month as of October 20, 2026.
 2.) Premium turnover has more strength - Premium turnover, which contributes 60% of BSE’s revenue, has reached a market share of over 30%, indicating further room for growth given BSE’s around 50% share in notional turnover.
 Also read: Nifty's PEG ratio near 10-year low but why don't stocks look cheap yet? Valuation paradox explained 
The P/N ratio has improved significantly from 6-7 bps in 2023-24 to 8-11 bps in 2025 and around 14 bps currently, reflecting a growing trend towards trading longer-term contracts. However, it remains below NSE’s ratio of over 20 bps.
Factors that could drive BSE’s P/N ratio higher include wider institutional participation supported by colocation expansion, an increase in higher-premium longer-dated expiry contracts to reduce the concentration of volumes on expiry days, and new products offering more monthly expiry contracts. Higher-premium stock options could also gain traction, given their P/N ratio of 120-150 bps on NSE, once NSE enters the F&O segment.
 3.) Beyond derivatives - BSE’s cash market share has risen from a plateau of around 7% to 9% over the past two months, with cash average daily traded turnover (ADTO) reaching a new quarterly high of Rs 105 billion in Q2FY27. The growth was supported by the introduction of a single contract note, implementation of smart order routing and the exclusive listing of popular stocks such as NSE and NSDL.
The number of cash market members increased to 829 in September 2026 from 806 a year earlier, while the number of unique client codes (UCCs) traded hit a record 6.16 million during the month, reflecting rising participation on the platform.
Cash market volumes are expected to grow further, driven by wider adoption of smart order routing and a ramp-up in NSE’s ADTO following the expiry of its lock-in period in March 2027.
 4.) Robust margin ahead - BSE’s EBITDA margin expanded from 9% in FY21 to over 65% in FY26, driven by a 57% revenue CAGR over FY21-26.
Around 45% of its expenses are fixed, while the remaining 55% are activity-dependent. These include clearing house expenses, which vary with the number of derivative contracts, and regulatory costs, which are linked to derivatives notional turnover.
While a slowdown in volumes could weigh on revenue growth, the impact on profitability should be partly offset by lower clearing house and regulatory expenses.
The brokerage expects EBITDA margins to reach 70%, supported by a 23% revenue CAGR over FY26-28, translating into a 27% CAGR in profit after tax (PAT) over the same period.
“We expect BSE to witness a strong recovery in volume growth, aided by rising member participation an improving P/N ratio. An improved growth trajectory in the cash segment, robust demand for co-location, and the strong positioning of the Star MF platform will also contribute to the company’s performance,” the brokerage said in a note.
The brokerage raised its revenue estimates by 8%/10% and PAT estimates by 10%/12% for FY27/FY28, respectively, factoring in the strong volume run-rate, the potential benefit from the CAS reversal and higher cash market volumes following NSE’s listing. A sustained recovery in volumes and further improvement in the premium-to-notional ratio could provide additional support.

docs.title: Tonbo Imaging shares soar another 17% after a 64% listing pop. Buy, sell or hold the stock?
docs.text:
Shares of newly-listed Tonbo Imaging rallied as much as 17% to their day’s high of Rs 1,331 on the BSE on Monday, extending Friday’s debut-day gains, when the stock listed at a 64% premium over the issue price.
 Tonbo Imaging India had fixed the IPO price band at Rs 665–Rs 700 per share. The issue opened for subscription on October 15 and closed on October 19, 2026, receiving an overall subscription of 132.81 times. The retail investor portion was subscribed 31.11 times, while the qualified institutional buyer (QIB) category, excluding anchor investors, saw 293.56 times subscription. The non-institutional investor (NII) portion was subscribed 156.36 times.
 Should you buy, sell or hold Tonbo Imaging shares?
 Ravi Singh , Chief Research Officer at Master Capital Services, said the key factors to track will be whether the company can sustain revenue growth, improve profitability and execute its growth plans while maintaining healthy working capital and operating cash flows.
“Long-term investors may continue to monitor the company’s defence electronics and imaging technology business, supported by demand for advanced surveillance, thermal imaging and defence modernisation solutions,” Singh said. Rather than focusing solely on its listing-day performance, investors may track quarterly revenue growth, order execution, EBITDA margins, order book development and operating cash flows to assess the company’s long-term growth prospects.
 About Tonbo Imaging
Incorporated in December 2003, Tonbo Imaging India Ltd . is a global defence electronics original equipment manufacturer (OEM) that designs, develops and manufactures advanced electro-optic and infrared (EO/IR), embedded vision, communication, guidance and surveillance systems for defence and security applications. Its product portfolio includes thermal imaging systems, weapon sights, missile seekers, fire control and missile guidance systems, targeting solutions and handheld thermal imaging devices.
 Live Events
The company caters to defence and security organisations across 24 countries, with more than 28,000 systems deployed in the field. According to the company, it is India’s largest manufacturer of thermal imaging systems for government and defence agencies and the country’s largest exporter of such systems by volume, based on FY24–FY26 data. As of June 30, 2026, Tonbo Imaging India had 339 permanent employees across functions including product design and development, manufacturing, project management, sales, finance, human resources and management.
Tonbo Imaging India raised Rs 255 crore from anchor investors by allotting 36.48 lakh equity shares at Rs 700 apiece, the upper end of the IPO price band.

docs.title: Swiggy shares jump 5% a day after Q2 results sparked a 17% crash. Why brokerages remain bullish despite ta
docs.text:
Swiggy shares jumped nearly 5% on Monday, a session after crashing nearly 17% following its Q2 results, which spooked investors and prompted brokerages to cut their target prices, even as they retained bullish ratings on the food delivery and quick commerce major.
 Swiggy shares rose to Rs 184.35 apiece on Monday morning. This came after the stock tumbled to a lifetime low of Rs 174.95 apiece on Friday, more than half of the record high level of Rs 434 the stock had hit less than a year ago in October 2025.
The sharp selloff on Friday was triggered after Swiggy announced its Q2 results for the second quarter of FY27. The company’s overall net loss narrowed to Rs 922 crore, from Rs 1,092 crore in the same quarter of last year. However, the rising losses in the quick commerce segment, Instamart, spooked investors, offsetting food delivery’s strong gains.
 Also read | Swiggy Q2 Results: Loss narrows YoY to Rs 922 crore; revenue jumps 36% 
Instamart’s adjusted EBITDA loss widened to Rs 895 crore from Rs 849 crore a year earlier and Rs 778 crore in the June quarter, as the company stepped up investments to attract customers and improve order frequency. It added 69 net dark stores during the quarter to cater to the highly competitive market.
 Live Events
Swiggy's core food delivery business continued to improve profitability, with GOV increasing 17.7% year-on-year to Rs 10,054 crore. The segment reported its highest quarterly adjusted EBITDA of Rs 341 crore, up 42% from Rs 240 crore a year earlier.
 What brokerages expect for Swiggy?
 Jefferies maintained its stance that Swiggy is a high-risk, high-reward stock, while reducing its target price to Rs 330 apiece. It noted that the current share price does not fully reflect the value of the food delivery business and existing cash, while the company's performance remains lacklustre compared with market leader Eternal . The brokerage said reducing quick commerce losses is essential for value discovery, as this remains a key investor concern.
 Nomura also maintained its ‘Buy’ rating while slashing the target price to Rs 300, continuing to view food delivery as a cash-generating business for Swiggy. Bernstein reiterated its ‘Outperform’ rating, while noting that the contrast with Blinkit's performance is testing investor patience over Instamart's turnaround and path to profitability.
 Also read | Rs 9,000 crore wiped out in a day: Why Swiggy investors are losing patience with Instamart 
 Swiggy share price
Swiggy shares have dropped more than 20% in a week and 31% in a month, with the stock overall being down more than 53% in 2026 so far. The stock has overall fallen around 57% in one year.
The company has a market capitalisation of a little over Rs 50,320 crore.

docs.title: AI infrastructure investment: Musk's warning hits neocloud stocks as debt concerns mount
docs.text:
Synopsis
 Shares of neocloud companies have fallen significantly amid concerns about consolidation in the sector. Elon Musk warned that many neoclouds may face closures as they struggle with heavy debt burdens. Research firm Gartner suggested that a high percentage of these companies could cease operations by 2032. Investor anxiety has increased due to mounting losses and a heavy reliance on AI spending.
 Listen to this article in summarized format
 Listen 
 Shares of neocloud companies declined in premarket trading on Monday after Elon Musk said the sector could face consolidation and failures, adding to concerns over a widening gap between AI infrastructure investment and revenue generation.
CoreWeave, which has become a poster child for mounting concerns over heavy AI spending, led the declines with a 4.5% drop, while Nebius Group fell 3.4% and IREN dropped 3.3%.
Shares of Applied Digital and TeraWulf shed over 2% each, while Core Scientific lost 1.7%. 
In a social media post on Sunday, Musk said that neocloud companies would face significant consolidation and failures, adding that SpaceX would not buy any neocloud companies.
"200+ neoclouds are going to see guppy-level death and consolidation. Some will make it through, but not many," he said.
CoreWeave and Nebius were not immediately available for comment.
Musk was not alone in flagging the risks to the sector.
Earlier this month, research firm Gartner said CoreWeave was at the top of the 100-odd neoclouds most exposed to the increasing leverage, and added that 80% of the companies could cease independent operations by 2032.
Some brokerages expect AI spending to shoot past a trillion dollars next year, adding to investor concerns about the repercussions of severe dependence on debt, at a time when AI assets face rapid depreciation and markets price in more interest rate hikes by the Federal Reserve.
"There is too much debt," said Alberto Gallo, founder of hedge fund Andromeda Capital.
"It's been spent on the assumption of infinite demand and need for AI compute, and it has concentrated credit markets into one risk, paying investors very little."
Bonds of Nebius maturing in 2034 and those of CoreWeave expiring in 2033 have hit record lows on the concerns.
CoreWeave, Nebius, Applied Digital and TeraWulf have reported quarterly losses over the past one year, while IREN has not turned a profit in the past three quarters, raising scrutiny over profitability.
Shares of CoreWeave, Nebius and IREN have fallen more than 30% this month alone. Investors betting on their fall have raked in at least $6 billion in paper profits.

 Shares of IndusInd Bank gained 2% to Rs 853 on the BSE on Monday after the private lender posted a net profit of Rs 1,176 crore in the second quarter of FY27, as against a net loss of Rs 445 crore in the same period last year, although Jefferies cut the target price following the earnings print.
 IndusInd Bank released its results for the July-September quarter of the ongoing financial year 2027 on Friday. Its net interest income meanwhile increased 4% year-on-year (YoY) to Rs 4,569 crore during the quarter under review.
 Also read | IndusInd Bank Q2 Results: Lender posts profit of Rs 1,176 crore vs Rs 445 crore loss a year ago 
The private lender’s asset quality improved during the quarter, with gross non-performing assets (GNPA) declining to 2.73% of gross advances from 3.25% in the June quarter and 3.6% a year earlier. Net NPA declined to 0.83% from 0.95% in the preceding quarter and 1.04% in the corresponding period last year. The provision coverage ratio stood at 70.19% at the end of September, compared with 71.81% a year earlier.
Provisions and contingencies, excluding tax, declined 54% to Rs 1,223 crore from Rs 2,631 crore in the year-ago quarter. Fee and other income jumped 36% YoY to Rs 2,248 crore from Rs 1,651 crore, while net revenue increased 12.5% to Rs 6,817 crore from Rs 6,060 crore.
 Live Events
 Why did Jefferies cut target price for IndusInd Bank? 
Jefferies said IndusInd Bank’s profit, following a loss last year was ahead of estimates, supported by lower credit cost & better fee and treasury income. Loans grew by 11% YoY, NII by 4%, and asset quality continues to improve. The international brokerage sees levers to improve profitability through better PPoP, even as credit costs are near the bottom.
However, Jefferies lowered its earnings estimates for IndusInd Bank to factor in tighter banca fee rules and slightly higher credit costs, which led it to reduce the target price to Rs 1,130 from Rs 1,250 apiece. The latest target price implies an upside potential of more than 35% from the stock’s previous closing price of Rs 835 apiece on NSE.
Jefferies maintained its ‘Buy’ call on IndusInd Bank’s shares, and noted that the stock’s valuations are attractive at the current levels.
 Motilal Oswal on IndusInd Bank share price 
 Motilal Oswal Financial Services maintained its ‘Neutral’ rating on the shares of IndusInd Bank with a target price of Rs 1,050 apiece, implying nearly 26% upside potential from the stock’s previous closing price.
The domestic brokerage noted that the company’s net profit beat its estimates, driven by healthy NII growth and high other income. It said IndusInd reported a healthy quarter, supported by steady NII growth and high other income. Consequently, RoA improved to 0.87% from 0.63% adjusted for one-off in Q1 FY27, with the bank maintaining the target of an exit RoA of 1% by the end of FY27.
Other income improved QoQ on the back of improving business momentum, while opex declined YoY. NIM contracted 12bp QoQ to 3.23% vs 3.35% (adjusted for one-off) in Q1 FY27. Business momentum picked up QoQ due to FCNR (B)-related advances, led by strong growth in the commercial banking and mid-market segments, while unsecured retail book growth remained muted, Motilal Oswal noted. Deposit growth was driven by strong FCNR (B) mobilisation, partly utilised to retire high-cost wholesale funding, which brought the retail deposit share to 50% of total deposits.
The broad-based reduction in slippages enabled improvement in asset quality ratios. The bank expects loan growth to broadly track industry growth in FY27. Motilal Oswal Financial Services raised its FY27 earnings estimates by 19% and that for FY28 by 17%.
 Also read | Double-digit growth seen on corporate scoreboard in Q2, but bank, IT, pharma lag 
 IndusInd Bank share price 
 IndusInd Bank shares have fallen over 3% in one week and 8% in a month, with the stock overall being down more than 6% in 2026 so far.
While IndusInd Bank shares have gained 11% in a year, the stock has delivered negative returns of 41% in three years and 28% in five years. The company has a market capitalisation of nearly Rs 65,059 crore.

As preparations for the Union Budget 2026–27 gather pace, the groundwork underway signals a clear policy intent to accelerate domestic demand, revive private investment and generate employment, according to a budget note by Motilal Oswal Financial Services (MOFSL). The brokerage has identified five stocks across auto, agriculture, defence, financials and infrastructure themes, which it believes could deliver strong gains for investors.
 "The Budget is expected to focus on income-tax, GST, and customs simplification to enhance ease of doing business and support fiscal consolidation, alongside targeted support for agriculture, MSMEs, manufacturing, infrastructure, higher defence capex, EVs, and renewables through credit and incentives," the note authored by Research Analysts Sneha Poddar and Rekha Jaat said.
A strong capital expenditure thrust across highways, logistics, defence, rail freight corridors and connectivity is anticipated, complemented by emphasis on skilling, rural prosperity, women empowerment, AI adoption, climate action and digital finance to anchor India’s next phase of economic expansion, the note added.
The finance ministry started work on the Union Budget for 2026-27 from October 9 as per a circular issued by the Department of Economic Affairs (DEA).
The preparations come against the backdrop of an additional 50% US tariff on most Indian goods and other external headwinds. These have raised risks to India's growth and jobs outlook, prompting calls for stronger support to the export sector.
 Live Events
 5 stocks to buy: 
The stocks recommended by MOFSL are TVS Motor Company, UPL , Bharat Dynamics (BDL), M&M Financial Services and Dalmia Bharat , and each of these stocks has been assigned a 20% weight.
 1) TVS Motors: TVS Motors continues to outperform peers and is well-positioned to benefit from the budget’s push to boost domestic consumption and rural demand through higher allocations, income support, and infrastructure spending.
MOFSL said that improving rural sentiment, strong entry-level recovery and sustained two-wheeler demand will be key triggers. Moreover, the company's market share gains, easing discounts, and margin expansion will provide strong earnings visibility. The Apache and Ntorq maker remains its top pick in OEMs.
 2) UPL: The diversified agrochemical leader is well positioned to benefit from the union budget push riding on rural prosperity via higher agri credit, MSME support, and value-chain strengthening, lifting farmer incomes and crop-protection demand.
The company's strong points are stronger volumes, export tailwinds, improved working-capital discipline and post-bond-repayment balance-sheet strength, the brokerage note said. The company's rising focus on speciality chemicals supports solid 2HFY26 growth.
 3) Bharat Dynamics: Bharat Dynamics (BDL), a defence play, has a robust Rs 50,000 crore order pipeline over five years, with Rs 20,000 crore targeted in 2-3 years. This aligns with the expected defence capex surge and infra push.
The recent Rs 2.5 lakh crore DAC approvals for missiles, undersea warfare, and naval arms leverage BDL's tactical/strategic expertise, propelling FY31 turnover to Rs 100bn via indigenisation and lower provisions, the note said.
 4) M&M Financial Services: M&M Financial is poised for Union Budget 2026-27 benefits via rural prosperity, MSME credit, and employment focus, driving PV/tractor loan growth amid surging volumes from festive demand, GST cuts, and restocking.
The company targets Rs 3 lakh crore in assets under management (AUM) by 2030, which is at an 18-20% CAGR, bolstered by AI underwriting, lower credit costs, controlled opex, and margin stability for strong earnings visibility in retail portfolios.
 5) Dalmia Bharat: The cement company benefits from the budget’s infra capex surge, PMAY rural housing, and urban projects, driving cement volume growth.
Dalmia Bharat is a low-cost cement producer with high blending ratios, green power and low freight. The company is targeting 62 mtpa capacity by FY28, and its cost optimisation endeavours will likely lift EBITDA margins amid sector consolidation.

The markets worldwide are waiting with bated breath on what will be a historic policy announcement from the US Federal Reserve , where the central bank is expected to usher in a rate cut cycle.
 The announcement will be made at 11:30 pm IST (Indian Standard Time) on Wednesday.
If analysts are to be believed, the US Fed is all but certain to cut interest rates for the first time in more than four years.
However, there is no consensus on the quantum of reduction. Some are predicting a smaller cut of a quarter of a percentage point, while others believe a bigger half-point reduction is in the works.
Senior officials at the US central bank, including Powell, have indicated that a rate cut is coming, as inflation eases toward the bank's long-term target of 2%, and the labour market continues to cool in the post-Covid economy.
 Live Events
If the Fed starts the rate cut cycle, the Reserve Bank of India is also expected to follow suit.
A smaller cut would be a more predictable move, while a bigger cut would do more to boost demand — while also running the risk of reigniting inflation.

— Federal Reserve (@federalreserve) September 18, 2024 
By the end 2024, markets are expecting a total reduction of at least 100 basis points in the first rate cut cycle in over 4 years since 2020.
But whether the Fed goes for 25 or 50 bps, the biggest trigger for stock prices to move up or down would be Powell's motivation behind the cut.
Asset classes from stocks, currencies and fixed income could all log swings in the immediate aftermath of the Fed decision.
While easing US interest rates are directionally positive for equities in general, “we should keep in mind interest rates are just one variable in a complex adaptive system that determines the direction of Indian equity markets”, said Anoop Vijaykumar, Investments and Head of Research at Capitalmind.

 Godrej Properties has corrected 26% year to date, compared with a 13% decline in the Nifty 50

Shares of Godrej Properties were up 1.93% on the NSE on October 26 after Nomura upgraded the stock to 'Buy' from 'Neutral', saying the risk-reward had turned attractive following a sharp correction.
The stock was trading at Rs 1,525.40 at 11:37 am. Nomura lowered its target price to Rs 1,900 from Rs 2,100.
Godrej Properties has corrected 26% year to date, compared with a 13% decline in the Nifty 50. In its October 25 report, Nomura said the company should consistently deliver around 15% pre-sales growth, supported by its ability to drive sales across regions and price points, leading to continued market share gains. It also expects the company to consistently generate free cash flow (FCF) from FY28, moderating the pace of net debt growth.
Godrej Properties trades at a premium of around 25% to net asset value (NAV), against Nomura's expectation of around 60%. "This suggests the stock has priced in most of the negatives," the brokerage said. It lowered its sum-of-the-parts-based target price, factoring in a higher weighted average cost of capital of 13.5%, against 12.5% previously, to account for ongoing volatility. A key risk is a slowdown in India's real estate market due to a prolonged Middle East war.
 Godrej Properties reported pre-sales of Rs 80 billion in Q2FY27, ahead of Nomura's estimate of Rs 73 billion. Sustenance sales of around Rs 50 billion contributed about 63% of pre-sales, while new launch sales stood at around Rs 30 billion.
Collections rose 31% year on year to Rs 53 billion, while operating cash flow increased 33% to around Rs 15.8 billion.
Revenue rose 161% year on year to Rs 19.4 billion, while EBITDA declined 9% to Rs 4.7 billion and profit after tax fell 62% to Rs 1.5 billion. Nomura attributed the EBITDA decline to accounting distortions at a project where profits had already been booked historically and settlement costs related to the Godrej Air project in Gurugram.
 Nomura expects FY27 pre-sales target to be met 
Godrej Properties achieved 43% of its FY27 pre-sales guidance of Rs 390 billion in the first half, leaving Rs 223 billion to be generated in the second half. Nomura estimates scheduled launches worth around Rs 320 billion in H2FY27 could generate pre-sales of Rs 140-160 billion. Sustenance sales of Rs 80-100 billion could help the company meet its target.
Collections and operating cash flow are expected to record around 15% CAGR over FY26-28, Nomura said. The company achieved around 40% of its FY27 collection guidance of Rs 240 billion in the first half, with collections up 25% year on year.
Nomura expects collections and operating cash flow to reach Rs 300 billion and Rs 110 billion, respectively, in FY28, with around 20% year-on-year growth. Given annual new land costs of Rs 85-90 billion, the brokerage expects Godrej Properties to turn FCF-positive in FY28, moderating net debt growth. Revenue recognition is also expected to contribute from FY28, supporting profit and equity recognition and helping the net debt-to-equity ratio peak out.

 Stock market recap: India's benchmark equity indices Sensex and Nifty rose on Monday, snapping a four-day losing streak, supported by value buying and gains in metal, telecom and healthcare stocks.
 The 30-share Sensex gained 482.92 points, or 0.66%, to settle at 73,606.75, recovering from early losses. The NSE Nifty rose 153.20 points, or 0.68%, to close at 22,753.20, ending its four-session decline.
 Among the 30 Sensex constituents, Adani Ports was the top gainer, rising 2.72%. Eternal gained 2.56%, followed by Kotak Mahindra Bank (2.53%), Trent (1.73%), Tata Steel (1.52%), Bharti Airtel (1.43%), InterGlobe Aviation (1.39%) and ITC (1.24%).
 Bajaj Finance, HDFC Bank , Maruti Suzuki, HCL Technologies and Power Grid were among the laggards.
 Two stock recommendations by MarketSmith India: 
 Buy: Apollo Micro Systems Limited (current price: ₹ 411) 
 Why it’s recommended: Strong order book growth and rising defence indigenisation spending position the company to benefit from large missile, torpedo, electronic warfare, and weapon-system programs with long revenue visibility. Capacity expansion, backward integration acquisitions, and transition from subsystem supplier to integrated weapon-systems manufacturers can drive higher revenue scale and margin expansion. 
 Key metrics: P/E: 106.27, 52-week high: ₹ 466.50, volume: ₹ 2,168.37 crore 
 Technical analysis: Reclaimed 200 EMA 
 Risk factors: High dependence on government defence contracts exposes the company to tender delays, policy changes, budget fluctuations, and order concentration risk. Rising working-capital requirements, debt-funded expansion, and execution risks on a growing order backlog could pressure cash flows and profitability. 
 Buy: ₹ 407–413 
 Target price: ₹ 480 in two to three months 
 Stop loss: ₹ 390 
 Buy: Dr. Reddy's Laboratories Limited (current price: ₹ 1,310) 
 Why it’s recommended: Diverse global generics franchise, strong API integration, and expanding biosimilars/specialty portfolio provide multiple long-term growth avenues across regulated and emerging markets. Growth in India and emerging markets, along with new complex generic and specialty drug launches, can support sustained revenue and earnings expansion. 
 Key metrics: P/E: 37.19, 52-week high: ₹ 1,414.90, volume: ₹ 1,285.42 crore 
 Technical analysis: Tight range breakout 
 Risk factors: Intense pricing pressure in the U.S. generics market and dependence on successful new product launches can adversely impact margins and growth. Regulatory compliance issues, FDA inspections, patent litigation, or delays in biosimilar/specialty drug approvals could affect financial performance. 
 Buy at: ₹ 1,297–1,317 
 Target price: ₹ 1,500 in two to three months 
 Stop loss: ₹ 1,220 
 How Nifty 50 performed 
 Indian equity markets ended Monday’s session higher, with the Nifty 50 gaining 153.20 points, or 0.68%, to close at 22,753.20, as buying interest returned after the recent correction. The index opened at 22,524.40, fell to an intraday low of 22,387.35 and recovered to finish at the day’s high, signalling strong buying momentum towards the close.
 Market breadth was positive, with 2,063 stocks advancing, 1,525 declining and 93 remaining unchanged, translating into an advance-decline ratio of 1.35:1. Sectoral performance was broadly positive, led by Nifty Metal (+2.21%), MidSmall Healthcare (+2.19%), Healthcare (+1.77%), Pharma (+1.76%) and Oil & Gas (+1.35%). IT (+0.87%) and Private Banks (+0.63%) also advanced, while Media (-0.34%) and Consumer Durables (-0.21%) ended lower.
 The Nifty formed a bullish daily candle, recovering sharply from its intraday low and closing at the day’s high. The rebound suggests renewed buying interest, although the broader trend remains bearish, with the index trading below key medium- and long-term moving averages and the prevailing downtrend still intact. The index has reclaimed its short-term moving average near 22,715, pointing to an improvement in near-term momentum, but a sustained recovery is needed to confirm a meaningful trend reversal.
 Momentum indicators also showed signs of improvement. The Relative Strength Index (RSI) rose to 46.08, moving above its signal average of 41.56, although it remained below the neutral 50 mark. The Moving Average Convergence Divergence (MACD) stood at -157.18, above its signal line at -209.54, indicating a bullish crossover. Its histogram turned positive at 52.36, although both the MACD and signal line remained in negative territory.
 From a technical perspective, the 22,500–22,400 range remains a key support zone. A decisive break below this area could trigger fresh selling pressure, potentially pulling the index towards 22,200–22,000. On the upside, the 23,000–23,200 range is likely to act as a significant resistance zone following the recent breakdown from these levels.
 How did the Nifty Bank perform? 
 Nifty Bank snapped a four-day losing streak on Monday, rising 79.35 points, or 0.15%, to close at 54,366.70 after recovering sharply from an intraday low of 53,777.50. The index remained in the red for much of the session, with PSU banks leading the early losses, before afternoon buying lifted it nearly 600 points from the day’s low.
 Kotak Mahindra Bank led the gainers, rising about 2.4% after reporting a 29% increase in quarterly profit and improved asset quality. Nifty 50 fell 87.65 points, or 0.39%, to close at 22,600, after sliding to an intraday low of 22,372, while Sensex slipped 125.56 points, or 0.17%, to settle at 73,123.83.

IT was the best-performing sector, with TCS, Infosys, HCL Tech, and Tech Mahindra rising, as investors bought Indian software firms despite overnight losses in U.S. tech giants such as Meta and Nvidia. Metals and Realty were the weakest sectors, with Tata Steel and Hindalco falling about 3% each, while Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles, Jio Financial Services, and NTPC also declined.
 The Bank Nifty fell 1.16%. Selling was far heavier in midcap and smallcap stocks, and breadth was deeply negative, with only 624 stocks advancing, 3,011 stocks declining, and 89 remaining unchanged. Crude oil, foreign flows, and quarterly earnings will remain in focus next week.
 Two stock recommendations by MarketSmith India:

Meanwhile, Seema Srivastava, Senior Research Analyst at SMC Global Securities, also highlighted HCLTech’s operating momentum and TCS’s scale, profitability and AI-led growth opportunities.
Garg said HCLTech deserves attention because of its improved growth guidance, while TCS remains relevant for investors seeking exposure to a large, diversified IT services business with a strong contract pipeline and expanding AI capabilities.
“HCLTech stands out for improving growth visibility, while TCS remains a strong candidate for investors seeking scale and long-term AI opportunities,” Garg said.
He added that Tech Mahindra could appeal to investors comfortable with higher execution risk, given its strong quarterly growth, although the sustainability of its turnaround remains an important consideration.
Srivastava highlighted HCLTech’s strong operating performance and TCS’s combination of scale, cash generation and relatively stronger margins.
HCLTech could appeal to growth-oriented investors because of its improved guidance and margin expansion. TCS, meanwhile, may suit investors prioritising business scale, profitability and exposure to long-term AI-led opportunities.
However, investors should assess both companies’ valuations and earnings expectations before taking fresh positions. Strong quarterly results do not automatically mean a stock is attractively valued.
Tech Mahindra could be considered by investors willing to accept higher risk in pursuit of a potential turnaround. Its strong revenue and profit growth, improving EBIT and deal wins indicate better operating momentum.
However, the recovery needs to be sustained across multiple quarters. Investors should monitor margin expansion, deal wins and the consistency of revenue growth to determine whether the improvement represents a durable recovery rather than a one-quarter rebound.
For Infosys, the central issue is whether its large deal wins and AI-led demand can offset the impact of slower revenue growth and the reduced FY27 guidance. Investors should watch constant-currency revenue growth, deal conversion and operating margins for signs of stabilisation.
Wipro warrants greater caution because of its weak deal bookings and subdued revenue outlook. A sustained improvement in bookings, revenue growth and profitability would strengthen its investment case.
For investors already holding these stocks, the latest results should be assessed alongside their original investment thesis, current valuations and expected earnings trajectory rather than prompting an automatic buy or sell decision.
“Ultimately, buy decisions should also consider current valuations, risk tolerance and investment horizon; quarterly performance alone does not establish which stock offers the best return,” Srivastava added.

According to Jigar S. Patel, Senior Manager of Equity Technical Research at Anand Rathi Share and Stock Brokers, a pullback after such a sharp advance was anticipated. However, Patel underscored an important development has emerged on the hourly chart of the Relative Strength Index (RSI).
"During the recent rally, the hourly RSI crossed the crucial 70 mark for the first time since August 2026. Despite the subsequent correction of approximately 700 points, the indicator has continued to hold above 40, suggesting that underlying momentum remains relatively resilient," Patel said.
"We maintain our buy-on-dips strategy, provided the Nifty holds above 22,200 on a daily closing basis. A decisive close below this level would weaken the bullish outlook," Patel said.
For Bank Nifty, Patel said an extended bottom formation accompanied by bullish RSI divergence on the hourly chart indicates a possible weakening of selling pressure.
"Going ahead, the 54,000–53,800 zone will be critical for sustaining the recovery outlook. On the upside, a sustained move above 55,000 could trigger further gains towards 56,000. However, a breakdown below 53,800 would weaken the bullish outlook," said Patel.
 One 97 Communications (Paytm) | Sell between ₹ 1,630 and ₹ 1,635 | Target price: ₹ 1,500 | Stop-loss: ₹ 1,690
According to Patel, Paytm is showing signs of weakness after decisively breaching the crucial support levels of ₹ 1,640 and ₹ 1,620 on a closing basis.
The breakdown indicates a deteriorating price structure and raises the possibility of further downside in the near term.
"The Relative Strength Index (RSI) on the 2-hour and 3-hour charts has already slipped below the 30 mark, signalling intense selling pressure. "Any recovery towards ₹ 1,630– ₹ 1,635 could provide an opportunity to sell, with a stop-loss at ₹ 1,690 and a downside target of ₹ 1,500," he said.
 Sapphire Foods | Buy | Target price: ₹ 221 | Stop-loss: ₹ 180
Sapphire Foods is trading near its previous demand zone, where buying interest has emerged over the last three to four trading sessions.
"The ₹ 185– ₹ 190 range has acted as a crucial support zone, with the stock managing to hold this area despite recent selling pressure. This indicates that buyers are attempting to defend the lower levels," said Patel.
From a technical perspective, a bullish divergence is visible on the daily chart based on the 7–8 period Relative Strength Index (RSI). This setup suggests that the underlying selling momentum may be weakening, raising the possibility of a short-term recovery.
"The combination of support near the previous demand zone and improving momentum strengthens the bullish outlook," Patel said.
"Considering these technical factors, the stock offers a potential buying opportunity with a stop-loss at ₹ 180 and an upside target of ₹ 221. A sustained hold above the ₹ 185– ₹ 190 zone will be important for the anticipated recovery," said Patel.
L&T | Target price: ₹ 3,900 | Stop loss: ₹ 3,550
Patel pointed out Larsen & Toubro (L&T) is showing signs of base formation near the crucial ₹ 3,600 level, which is emerging as a strong support zone.
This level coincides with the monthly Camarilla support and a previous demand zone, where buying interest had emerged earlier. The confluence of these technical factors strengthens the possibility of a recovery from current levels.
The Relative Strength Index (RSI) is holding just above the oversold zone, indicating that selling pressure may be easing. If the stock sustains above ₹ 3,600, a rebound towards ₹ 3,900 cannot be ruled out.
However, a decisive breakdown below this support could weaken the technical structure.
"Considering the favourable risk-reward setup near the support zone, traders may consider buying L&T with a stop-loss of ₹ 3,550 and a target of ₹ 3,900," said Patel.

AU Small Finance Bank share price opened at ₹ 884 per share today, as compared to the previous close of ₹ 932.90 on Friday and touched an intraday low of ₹ 845.40. Meanwhile, Ujjivan Small Finance Bank share price opened at ₹ 57.60 on NSE today, as compared to the previous close of ₹ 58.10 last week. The banking stock touched an intraday low of ₹ 54.44 today.
Both small finance stocks fell sharply after Sensex and Nifty 50 dropped in early trade on Monday.
AU Small Finance Bank reported a 53% year-on-year increase in net profit to ₹ 858 crore for the second quarter ended September 30, 2026, supported by higher interest income. The bank had recorded a net profit of ₹ 561 crore in the corresponding quarter of the previous financial year.
The lender’s total income rose to ₹ 6,382 crore in the September quarter, compared with ₹ 5,224 crore in the year-ago period, according to a regulatory filing.
Interest income increased to ₹ 5,612 crore during the quarter under review from ₹ 4,511 crore in the same quarter last year.
AU Small Finance Bank’s net interest income (NII) rose 32% year-on-year to ₹ 2,820 crore in the July-September quarter, compared with ₹ 2,144 crore in the corresponding quarter of the previous year.
[Ujjivan Small Finance Bank](https://scanx.trade/company/ujjivan-small-finance-bank-ltd) reported its highest-ever quarterly profit after tax (PAT) of ₹ 365 crore in Q2 FY27, with return on assets (ROA) improving to 2.4% from 2.2% in the preceding quarter.
The bank’s net interest income (NII) rose 35% year-on-year to ₹ 1,244 crore, supported by a net interest margin (NIM) of 8.4%. Despite an increase in fresh slippages, asset quality remained stable, with gross non-performing assets (GNPA) at 2.1% and net NPA at 0.31%.
Total income stood at ₹ 2,450 crore, reflecting strong revenue growth driven by expansion in the bank’s asset base. Ujjivan Small Finance Bank retained its FY27 asset quality guidance of 2.0-2.2%, even as fresh slippages rose to ₹ 350 crore in Q2 FY27 from ₹ 170 crore in the previous quarter.
The bank’s gross loan book grew 32.1% year-on-year to ₹ 45,699 crore, while total deposits increased 29.2% to ₹ 50,643 crore. Current account and savings account (CASA) deposits accounted for 26% of the total deposit base. Meanwhile, secured lending segments contributed 52.1% of the loan book, while the unsecured micro banking portfolio expanded by around 6% in the first half of FY27.
Global brokerage firm Jefferies has given a ‘buy’ rating to AU Small Finance Bank stock, with a target price of ₹ 1,250, seeing an upside potential up to 34%.

Slippages were tad higher than our estimate, but credit costs were lower due to a fall in the coverage ratio; the bank has also written off more loans. Transition to Universal Bank will strengthen deposit franchise and grading. We lower est. by 1-5% for FY27-29 & see 28% CAGR in profit over FY27-29, so stays in our 25% CAGR Club,” said the brokerage firm.

“The stock has immediate support in the ₹ 53–50 zone, which will be crucial to watch for downside protection. On the upside, resistance is placed at ₹ 60, followed by ₹ 63 and ₹ 66. docs.title: Reliance shares: Why is it wise to buy RIL shares amid a falling stock market — Explained with 3 reasons; target price
docs.text:
According to stock market experts, shares of Reliance Industries Ltd (RIL) are under pressure due to weak trends on Dalal Street. They said that the company's fundamentals are very strong, and amid the ongoing Middle East crisis and soaring crude oil prices, there is a need for top-quality oil refiners, and RIL fits this category. The US Secretary of State Marco Rubio's meeting with Mukesh Ambani should be seen from this angle. They said that Reliance's Jio Platforms value unlock will also benefit RIL, as it holds around two-thirds of the company's share capital. Pointing to the third reason for buying Reliance shares amid the current fall in the Indian stock market, experts said that the US-Iran war has fueled crude oil prices, but diesel prices have surged even more. RIL is a diesel exporter and is expected to reap this benefit as well.
Pointing towards the US Secretary of State Marco Rubio meeting Mukesh Ambani, Avinash Gorakshkar, Founder of Avinash Mentor Research, said, “Though it is no official confirmation, but Marco Rubio meeting Mukesh Ambani is expected to focus on the refining business, as a good number of refiners have gone out of business in the Middle East due to the prolonged US-Iran war. After the regime change in Venezuela, crude oil production is expected to jump from the current 1 million barrels per day to around 2.5 million barrels per day. However, Venezuelan crude oil is thick, and only a limited number of refiners can process it; RIL is one of them. Reliance Industries is already refining the Ural crude oil, imported from Russia, which is almost the same as Venezuelan crude oil.”
Gorakshkar said that the market is pricing Venezuelan crude oil for RIL at a discount, as with Russia, which will strengthen RIL's refining business and lead to a healthy balance sheet for the company.
Pointing towards a catch behind the soaring crude oil prices, Anuj Gupta, a SEBI-registered market expert, said, “When the US-Iran war began, Brent Crude oil price was at $72 per barrel and diesel price in the international market was around $110 per barrel. Today, after nearly eight months of the US-Iran war, Brent Crude oil prices have risen to around $115 per barrel, while diesel prices have touched $200 per barrel. So, the gap between the crude oil and diesel oil price has widened from $38 per barrel to around $90 per barrel, a big surge in the business of the OMCs and oil refiners, which nobody is talking about amid soaring crude oil prices.”
On how Reliance Industries is expected to benefit from this big rise in the crude oil and diesel price gap in the international market, the SEBI-registered expert said that $100 per barrel has become a new normal for the markets and RIL is a big exporter of diesel in the international market. He said that Reliance Industries' diesel and refined fuel export business has transformed significantly post-Russia-Ukraine war, shifting from capturing early arbitrage margins on discounted Russian crude to navigating shifting Western sanctions, US diplomatic engagements, and changing global trade routes. Following the outbreak of the Russia-Ukraine war in 2022, Reliance's twin refineries in Jamnagar (Gujarat) capitalised on heavily discounted Russian Urals crude, deferring maintenance to maximise production and exports of diesel, jet fuel, and gasoline to energy-starved international markets.
“The market is expecting the benefit of value unlocking for RIL, as it holds around one-third stake in Reliance Jio Platforms. So, this rally in the RIL shares can be attributed to the Jio Platforms IPO subscription opening,” Avinash Gorakshkar said.
On how one can connect Jio Platforms IPO with Reliance Industries' shares. Avinnash Gorakshkar said that even after value unlock from RIL, the balance sheets of these two companies would be connected due to RIL's strong two-thirds shareholding. Good financial performance would continue to be reflected in RIL's balance sheet.
Expecting this value unlock rally to continue further, Avinash Gorakshkar said, “The market is estimating around ₹ 350 to ₹ 500 per share rise in RIL shares due to the value unlock. However, much will depend upon the kind of listing Jio Platforms IPO receives.”
Divulging the Jio Platforms IPO listing price, Avinash Gorakshkar said, “The market is expecting Jio Platforms IPO listing price in the range of ₹ 1350 to ₹ 1400, depending upon the market mood. This premium is expected to be added to RIL shares. The Jio Platforms IPO price band is ₹ 1,065 to ₹ 1,119. So, this ₹ 1350 to ₹ 1400 Jio Platforms IPO listing price means ₹ 250 to ₹ 300 per share addition in Reliance shares in the short-term-medium term. However, by the end of this fiscal, RIL share price is expected to end between ₹ 1,550 and ₹ 1,700, depending upon the kind of market mood that remains in the last quarter of the current fiscal.”
Decoding the technical chart of Reliance shares, Mahesh M Ojha, VP — Research and Business Development at KC Securities, said, “Reliance Industries shares have a strong base formation at the ₹ 1,145. The stock has broken out above ₹ 1,200 and is now heading towards the short-term target of ₹ 1,265. Existing shareholders and fresh buyers can initiate coverage with a strict stop-loss at ₹ 1,145 for the targets of ₹ 1,265, ₹ 1,290 and ₹ 1,350 in the short-term horizon.”

docs.title: Mint Explainer: How will Sebi’s relaxed margin rules help brokers?
docs.text:
Explainer Mint Explainer: How will Sebi’s relaxed margin rules help brokers? Apoorva Ajith 3 min read 26 Oct 2026, 01:07 PM IST Summary By eliminating additional margin collections on subsequent trades after early pay-in, Sebi's new rules aim to ease the capital burden on stockbrokers-particularly smaller firms-and streamline same-day cash market reinvestments. Gift this article Check your portfolio This is a Mint Premium article gifted to you. Subscribe to enjoy similar stories. Subscribe now The Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) has relaxed margin rules for investors who use proceeds from share sales to buy other stocks on the same day. The new rules aim to reduce brokers’ upfront funding burden when investors use proceeds from shares sold through the early pay-in (EPI) mechanism. Mint explains the changes and whether they will benefit brokers. What are the changes? In a circular issued on 22 October, India’s market regulator eased margin requirements for trades made using proceeds from shares sold through the EPI mechanism. EPI allows investors to transfer shares to the clearing corporation before the usual settlement deadline. Once the clearing corporation accepts the transfer request, the value of those shares can be considered for meeting certain margin requirements. Under the new rules, clearing corporations will not collect additional margins from trading or clearing members on a client's subsequent buy or sell positions, up to the value of the accepted EPI. The eligible amount will be the lower of the EPI value or the value of the shares sold. If an investor closes the original sale position, the EPI benefit will be withdrawn. Any resulting margin shortfall can then be blocked from the broker's own collateral. The new rules will take effect on 22 February 2027, four months after the circular was issued. Why were the changes needed? The changes address a gap in the existing margin framework. When an investor sells shares held in a demat account and completes EPI, the clearing corporation receives the shares early. This reduces the risk of settlement failure and allows the margin requirement for the sale to be released. However, if the investor uses the sale proceeds to buy another stock on the same day, the broker may still have to arrange the required upfront margin for the purchase. This can be around 20%, depending on the stock and applicable requirements. For example, if an investor sells shares worth ₹ 100 and uses the proceeds to buy another stock, the broker may have to set aside ₹ 20 from its own trading limits to meet the margin requirement. This creates a funding burden even though the sale proceeds are available. The change follows proposals from the Broker Industry Standards Forum and recommendations from Sebi's Risk Management Review Committee (RMRC). It aims to make better use of the value of shares already transferred for settlement, while retaining safeguards against margin shortfalls. Will the changes help brokers? The relaxation could particularly benefit smaller brokers , who may have limited funds or clearing limits to support clients who want to buy stocks on the same day using proceeds from share sales. Under the existing framework, brokers with greater financial resources have generally been better placed to offer same-day trading facilities. Smaller brokers may find it difficult to meet the margin requirements on new purchases, even when the investor has completed EPI for the shares sold. By reducing the need to provide additional margins for eligible trades, the new rules could help more brokers offer the facility. Investors may also be able to use their sale proceeds more efficiently instead of waiting for the next settlement day. The change builds on the EPI framework revision in October 2024. Before that revision, investors could generally use 80% of their sale proceeds on the trade day, with the remaining 20% becoming available after settlement on the following day. How will the new rules affect cash markets? The new rules will support participation in the cash market by making it easier for investors to move their funds between stocks on the same day. Lower margin requirements on eligible trades may also help brokers serve more clients without having to commit as much of their own collateral. The move comes amid a decline in cash-market activity. Average daily cash-market turnover on the National Stock Exchange ( NSE ) fell about 7% to ₹ 1.05 trillion in FY26 from ₹ 1.13 trillion in FY25. The market capitalization of the NSE cash segment also fell about 6% to ₹ 4.48 trillion between January and October, according to data from the exchange. The relaxation could make same-day trading more accessible, particularly for clients of smaller brokers. However, its impact on turnover will depend on how widely brokers adopt the facility and how investors respond. The changes do not guarantee a recovery in trading activity. She holds a postgraduate diploma in business and financial journalism from the Asian College of Journalism, where she developed a strong foundation in markets, companies, and economic policy. She began her journalism journey with an internship at Bloomberg, where she worked across beats such as real estate, infrastructure, capital markets, and deals, which helped her understanding of business and finance.

docs.title: AI takes centre stage in festive ads as brands seek faster, cheaper campaigns
docs.text:
News 
 AI takes centre stage in festive ads as brands seek faster, cheaper campaigns
 Neethi Lisa Rojan , Rudrani Chattopadhyay 4 min read 26 Oct 2026, 12:07 PM IST 
 Summary
 Brands are increasingly using artificial intelligence to produce more advertisements, adapt campaigns for regional audiences and reduce production time and costs. Yet, marketers concede human creativity remains central to effective storytelling. 
 Gift this article Check your portfolio 
 This is a Mint Premium article gifted to you.
Subscribe to enjoy similar stories.
 Subscribe now 
 This year's festive season is emerging as a key moment for the adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) in Indian advertising, with brands increasingly using the technology to produce campaign assets, test creative ideas and tailor messages to different audiences.
 The shift is being driven by the need to save time and costs during the busiest period for shopping and gifting. Advertising executives say AI allows brands to create multiple versions of a campaign without the expense of repeated studio shoots or the time-consuming production processes traditionally involved.
 Festive advertising accounts for about 34–35% of India's annual advertising expenditure, estimated at ₹ 60,000–62,000 crore, according to Datum Intelligence.
 Companies across segments, including Oppo, SBI Life Insurance, Haier and Eastern by Orkla India, have used AI-generated advertisements during the wedding season. The technology is emerging as an alternative to the big-budget productions that brands have traditionally relied on during the festive period.
 A traditional 30- to 90-second television commercial can cost ₹ 50 lakh or more, depending on its production requirements. “AI-generated advertising can cost a fraction of traditional production, although the actual savings depend on the script, complexity and quality expected,” said Preetham Venkky, chief digital officer at Omnicom Advertising India.
 “The induction of AI is no longer a matter of choice. It is almost the norm,” said Sandeep Goyal, chairman of Rediffusion. He said advances in AI-generated imagery and video have made it increasingly difficult for consumers to distinguish AI-generated advertisements from conventionally filmed ones.
 Cost savings
 AI is also influencing marketing budgets. Instead of spending heavily on a single production, companies can create multiple variations and spend more on other initiatives.
 “By bringing AI into early script ideation, packaging visualization and copy adaptations, we compressed weeks of back-and-forth into just a few days,” said Arvind Mediratta, founder and chief executive of FreshTerra, a food and grocery retail brand.
 FreshTerra has redirected the savings from reduced spending on physical samples and early design iterations towards in-store experiences, its direct-from-farmer supply chain and local visibility, Mediratta said.
 Ferns N Petals (FNP), the gifting and floral retailer, has also adopted a combination of human and AI-led production. “Our speed of creative execution has increased by nearly 4X, allowing us to develop, test and deploy a much larger volume of creatives in a fraction of the time,” said Avi Kumar, the company’s chief marketing officer.
 FNP has seen better click-through rates—the share of people who click on an advertisement after seeing it—while return on advertising spend has remained broadly stable.
 Beauty brand RENÉE Cosmetics has reported higher engagement and lower production time for its AI-generated advertisements. “In our campaigns, AI-generated ads have delivered 30.16% higher engagement rates compared with conventional creatives, while helping reduce production time by an estimated 70–80%,” Priyank Shah, co-founder of RENÉE Cosmetics, said.
 The company also reported a 10–20% reduction in cost per result—the cost of achieving a desired outcome, such as a click or purchase—in campaigns where the data supported such a range, Shah said. The figures suggest potential gains in both creative output and cost efficiency, although results may vary across campaigns.
 Still, advertising executives caution against treating AI as a substitute for creative judgment. Consumers may respond to an advertisement because of its story and relevance, rather than the technology used to produce it.
 Venkky said AI could work across categories, from fashion and beauty to food and jewellery. The deciding factor is whether the technology suits the creative idea. Products that depend on accurate representation, such as jewellery , luxury goods and food, require particular care.
 Sam Mahandru, founder of IndoBevs, the beverage company behind BroCode, said the starting point for any brand extension or creative campaign should be consumer preferences rather than the technology used to produce it.
 “The festive season is one of the most crowded times in the consumer space, and a bigger budget doesn’t automatically buy more attention. Whatever the time of year, what matters most is whether our consumers can relate to our campaigns,” Mahandru said.
 He cited the company’s work on the campaigns ‘Unhinged India’ and ‘BroTection’, which he said draw on Indian subcultures and consumer concerns. Its in-house brand team is exploring AI and other tools to speed up production and test different creative approaches, he added.
 “In that sense, AI supports our creative thinking and process. We judge every campaign the same way: by how well it reflects our consumers’ deepest thoughts and aspirations,” Mahandru said.
 For advertisers, therefore, AI's immediate advantage may lie more in the speed and scale of production than in making every campaign more effective.

Mint Money 
 Soaring domestic and international airfares make travellers rethink year-end holidays
 Shipra Singh 6 min read 26 Oct 2026, 01:53 PM IST 
 Summary
 Domestic airfares are 30-40% higher than a year ago as fuel costs, a weaker rupee and limited flight capacity squeeze festive travel budgets. 
 Gift this article Check your portfolio 
 This is a Mint Premium article gifted to you.
Subscribe to enjoy similar stories.
 Subscribe now 
 For Mumbai-based Soumi Pal, flying her parents down from Kolkata for their annual visit has become an expensive affair this year. She typically pays ₹ 30,000 for their combined return airfares, but this year, tickets are costing upwards of ₹ 20,000 per person. She has scrapped the flight journey and worked out an elaborate train itinerary instead.
 Her parents will travel from Kolkata to Varanasi by overnight train, while she will join them from Mumbai. The three will spend two days holidaying in Varanasi before returning together to Mumbai by first-class AC train.
 “Even with the holiday thrown in, I am paying considerably less for the train journeys than what I would have spent just flying them to Mumbai and back,” she said.
 Like Pal, many travellers are reworking their plans this year, whether to visit family during the festive break or take a holiday in December, as airfares soar. According to data from Yatra Online, domestic airfares are currently 30-40% higher than a year ago. Rising aviation fuel prices amid the West Asia war have been a key driver of the increases, compounded by the rupee's consistent depreciation over the past year.
 “The rupee crossed 90 to the dollar in early December last year, went past 93 in March and has been past 94 since. Airlines pay for fuel, aircraft leases and maintenance in dollars, so a weaker rupee feeds straight into the ticket,” said Prashant Daroch, founder of Atravelq, a travel company offering personalized international holidays.
 Bharatt Malik, executive vice-president, consumer business, Yatra Online, said that several domestic airlines had reduced flight frequencies on certain routes to contain costs. The resulting capacity reductions contributed to higher fares. The combination of expensive fuel, fewer flights and a depreciating rupee has made the December holiday season particularly costly.
 Fuel and fares
 Aviation turbine fuel ( ATF ), which ordinarily accounts for around 35-40% of an airline's operating expenses, has become considerably more expensive amid the West Asia war. After repeated hikes in ATF prices, the Federation of Indian Airlines estimates that fuel now accounts for 55-60% of operating costs. Airlines have repeatedly revised fuel surcharges since April as a result.
 The impact is being felt across domestic routes.
 “The increase has been broadly similar across busy metro routes and those connecting cities such as Kolkata, Lucknow, Ahmedabad and Pune. Fares to leisure destinations such as Goa, Kerala and Rajasthan have also risen in line with the broader trend, with sharper spikes expected around peak travel dates during Christmas and New Year,” said Malik.
 For example, direct return flights from Delhi to Goa for the second half of December are selling at around ₹ 25,000 per person, compared with ₹ 15,000-20,000 last year, an increase of up to 67%. Other popular winter destinations, including Kerala and Rajasthan, are also witnessing higher fares. For larger families, the difference can quickly run into tens of thousands of rupees and squeeze holiday budgets. A family of four flying from Delhi to Goa would spend roughly ₹ 1 lakh on return tickets alone, against ₹ 60,000 last year.
 Higher operating costs are only part of the problem. Airlines cut flight frequencies on several routes earlier this year to manage expenses, and capacity has yet to fully recover.
 “Airlines are gradually restoring frequencies reduced earlier this year, but limited seat availability continues to push up fares,” said Malik.
 International squeeze
 International travellers are facing an even sharper increase. Besides higher fuel surcharges and reduced flight capacity, disruptions at West Asia transit hubs have affected connections to Europe and the US.
 Amar Kedia, founder of TravelBluez, a boutique travel agency that offers luxury packages, said airfares to European destinations, including Germany, Austria, the Netherlands and the Czech Republic, have risen 60-70%.
 “The corollary is that demand from these routes is shifting towards Southeast Asian destinations, pushing up airfares and hotel tariffs there as well.”
 Daroch added that, with West Asia disrupted by the war and airspace closures, much of the traffic that would have gone to Dubai or onward to Europe had swung to Southeast Asia.
 “Delhi-Bangkok return fares are currently ₹ 28,000-48,000 for December, compared with around ₹ 25,300 last Christmas. Delhi-Ho Chi Minh City returns have increased from ₹ 43,800 to ₹ 55,000-90,000, with the highest airfares for connecting flights during peak dates,” he said.
 For Bengaluru-based Devashish Sharma, 28, the cost of flying to Thailand has nearly tripled compared with his last trip. He paid ₹ 19,000 for non-stop return flights from Bengaluru last year during the off-season. This December, even flights involving stopovers are costing upwards of ₹ 55,000.
 “I was budgeting for ₹ 25,000-35,000 given it is peak season, but the fares are actually double,” he said. “I have shelved my December holiday plans looking at the airfare. I will travel in the off-shoulder season again when the fares are lower at around ₹ 35,000.”
 The soaring airfares may also change his travel habits beyond this holiday season.
 “I typically plan two international holidays annually, but I may reduce that to one and prioritize shoulder season travel until airfares rationalize.”

News Banks make slow progress in financial inclusion schemes, private lenders trail state-run peers Harsh Kumar , Manas Pimpalkhare 7 min read 26 Oct 2026, 07:07 PM IST Summary Private lenders trail state-run banks in Mudra disbursements, Vishwakarma loan sanctions and SVANidhi claims processing, raising questions over timely support for small businesses and informal workers. Gift this article Check your portfolio This is a Mint Premium article gifted to you. Subscribe to enjoy similar stories. Subscribe now Private-sector banks are lagging public-sector lenders in three government schemes for small entrepreneurs, artisans and street vendors, with gaps in credit disbursement, loan sanctions and the processing of interest-subvention claims, according to a government document reviewed by Mint and two people aware of the development. The gaps have emerged as beneficiaries face rising input costs amid global supply-chain disruptions linked to geopolitical conflicts, particularly the West Asia war. Wholesale price inflation rose to 11.31% in September from 9.92% in August, while retail inflation hit a 23-month high of 5.54%. A deficient monsoon is also expected to weigh on rural incomes. Queries emailed on 22 October to the finance, MSME and housing and urban affairs ministries, the Reserve Bank of India, the Indian Banks' Association, and public- and private-sector banks remained unanswered until press time on 26 October. PM Mudra: Private banks trail targets Under the Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana (PMMY), which provides credit to small and budding entrepreneurs, HDFC Bank, Yes Bank, IDBI Bank and Federal Bank disbursed just 24-30% of their fiscal year 2027 (FY27) annual targets in the first half, the document showed. HDFC Bank disbursed ₹ 9,065 crore against a ₹ 30,000-crore target; Yes Bank, ₹ 1,133 crore against ₹ 4,100 crore; IDBI Bank, ₹ 2,013 crore against ₹ 7,500 crore; and Federal Bank, ₹ 1,280 crore against ₹ 5,400 crore. Public-sector banks achieved 32-56% of their FY27 targets. State Bank of India (SBI) disbursed ₹ 27,976 crore, or 42% of its ₹ 66,600-crore target, while Indian Bank disbursed ₹ 5,102 crore, or 32% of its ₹ 15,950-crore target. Several state-run banks had achieved at least half their FY27 disbursal targets in the first half. Bank of India disbursed 56% of its ₹ 16,200-crore target ( ₹ 9,122 crore), followed by Union Bank of India at 54% ( ₹ 13,830 crore of ₹ 25,700 crore), Bank of Baroda at 53% ( ₹ 16,039 crore of ₹ 30,000 crore), Indian Overseas Bank at 52% ( ₹ 5,198 crore of ₹ 10,000 crore) and Bank of Maharashtra at 50% ( ₹ 4,025 crore of ₹ 8,000 crore). All figures are for H1 FY27. PM SVANidhi: Claims remain pending Under PM SVANidhi, which supports street vendors, private banks reduced pending interest-subvention claims by 14% to 187,595 at end-September from 213,064 at end-July. But progress was uneven: HDFC Bank cut its backlog by just 0.2% to 48,657, Federal Bank by 0.1% to 4,667 and Axis Bank by 0.03% to 15,497. Yes Bank, IndusInd Bank and ICICI Bank recorded no reduction. Some private lenders, however, made substantial progress. Kotak Mahindra Bank reduced its pending claims by 31% to 12,151, while IDFC First Bank cut its backlog by 85% to 149 from 987 over the same period. Public-sector banks cut pending claims by 39% to 5.89 million from 9.13 million over the same period. SBI alone reduced its backlog by 39% to 3.13 million from 5.02 million, the document showed. The gap also extended to loan sanctions. Between August 2025 and September 2026, public-sector banks sanctioned an average of 74% of street vendors' credit applications, against 20% for private banks. One of the government officials cited above said banks faced gaps in processing applications and clearing claims, including discrepancies between claims reported on the portal and those in banks' core banking systems. “While some banks have made progress in processing applications and clearing pending claims, others continue to face gaps in sanctioning and disbursal. In the case of PM SVANidhi, the mismatch between claims reported on the portal and banks’ core banking systems is also an issue that needs to be reconciled. The focus is on improving processing efficiency and ensuring that eligible beneficiaries receive timely credit,” the official said, requesting anonymity. PM Vishwakarma scheme: Public banks sanction more Under PM Vishwakarma, which provides credit to artisans and informal workers, public-sector banks sanctioned 44% of processed applications in the first half of FY27 — 539,349 of 1.21 million. Private banks sanctioned 36%, or 28,108 of 78,542 applications, the document showed. The scheme has an outlay of ₹ 13,000 crore for FY24-28. The lower participation of private banks in financial-inclusion schemes is not new, but structural gaps need attention, said Veeramani C, professor and director of the Centre for Development Studies, a Thiruvananthapuram-based think tank. “We need clear and transparent procedures. We need to ask if we can streamline these procedures to reduce compliances for banks and beneficiaries. Issues can arise in loan disbursements due to information asymmetry, where a potential beneficiary may not be aware of the paperwork required. At the same time, banks may not be willing to take risks currently,” he said.
