docs.title: Kotak Mahindra Bank: Why brokerages see up to 21% upside despite 22 bps drop in margins
docs.text: Kotak Mahindra Bank’s September-quarter performance has prompted Motilal Oswal, Jefferies and JM Financial to maintain a positive outlook on the lender, citing healthy loan growth, stronger net interest income and stable asset quality. The brokerages have highlighted the bank’s operating performance, deposit mobilisation and potential to deploy surplus liquidity as key factors supporting its earnings outlook. Motilal Oswal maintained its ‘Buy’ rating and set a target price of Rs 500, implying an upside potential of 16% from the market price of Rs 430 cited in its October 25 report. Jefferies also retained its ‘Buy’ rating and raised its target price to Rs 520 from Rs 460. JM Financial upgraded the stock to ‘Buy’ from ‘Add’ and raised its target price to Rs 500 from Rs 415. The bank reported standalone profit after tax of Rs 4,212 crore in Q2FY27, up 29% year on year and 2% quarter on quarter. Net interest income rose 16% year on year to Rs 8,460 crore, while net interest margins declined 22 basis points quarter on quarter to 4.31%, partly due to the impact of foreign currency non-resident bank (FCNR-B) deposits. Motilal Oswal on Kotak Mahindra Bank: ‘Buy’ Motilal Oswal retained its ‘Buy’ rating on Kotak Mahindra Bank and set a target price of Rs 500, implying an upside potential of 16%. In its October 25 report, the brokerage said the bank delivered a steady quarter, with healthy net interest income growth partly offset by higher provisions. Standalone profit after tax stood at Rs 4,212 crore, while consolidated profit after tax increased 26% year on year and 3% quarter on quarter to Rs 5,640 crore. ALSO READIndia’s factory boom needs more than factories: 2 stocks, one with 50%+ EBITDA margins Net interest income grew 16% year on year and 7% quarter on quarter to Rs 8,460 crore. Advances increased 25% year on year and 13% quarter on quarter to Rs 5.8 lakh crore. Excluding FCNR-B-related and Kotak Mahindra Investments Ltd (KMIL) loans, growth was 19% year on year and 8% quarter on quarter, supported by small and medium enterprise lending and corporate banking. Deposits grew 23% year on year and 14% quarter on quarter, helped by FCNR-B deposit mobilisation of Rs 55,300 crore. Current account and savings account (CASA) deposits declined 2% quarter on quarter, taking the CASA ratio down by 210 basis points to 38.2%. ALSO READInfosys vs TCS: Which IT stock offers better value after Q2? Deal wins, AI growth in focus The brokerage noted that fresh slippages declined to Rs 1,230 crore, down 7% quarter on quarter. Gross and net non-performing asset ratios improved by 14 and 3 basis points, respectively, to 1.04% and 0.24%. Credit costs declined to 0.35% from 0.46% in the previous quarter. Motilal Oswal raised its earnings estimates for FY27 and FY28 by 3% and 7%, respectively. It expects return on assets of 2.07% and return on equity of 12.5% in FY27. Margin pressure and liquidity deployment Motilal Oswal said net interest margins fell 22 basis points quarter on quarter to 4.31%, below its estimate of 4.43%. The decline was partly attributable to FCNR-B deposits and leverage, which accounted for 15 basis points of the impact. Day-count variations and repayment of inter-bank participation certificate borrowings accounted for the remainder. The brokerage said FCNR-B proceeds had partly funded the KMIL loan book, repaid high-cost deposits and reduced inter-bank participation certificate borrowings. The remaining funds are expected to be deployed over the coming quarters. Motilal Oswal expects margins to improve as the bank deploys surplus liquidity and benefits from the transmission of repo-rate changes. It also noted that around 60% of the loan book is linked to the repo rate, while floating-rate advances account for 65% to 70% of total advances. The bank’s operating profit before provisions and contingencies increased 21% year on year and 4% quarter on quarter to Rs 6,380 crore. Operating expenses rose 14% year on year and 3% quarter on quarter to Rs 5,270 crore. The brokerage also noted differences in the performance of the bank’s subsidiaries. Kotak Prime’s net earnings fell 29% quarter on quarter to Rs 250 crore, while Kotak Life’s profit after tax declined 41% quarter on quarter to Rs 200 crore. Kotak Securities’ reported profit after tax declined 35% quarter on quarter to Rs 350 crore, while Kotak Asset Management Company’s profit after tax fell 28% quarter on quarter to Rs 400 crore. Jefferies maintains ‘Buy’, raises target price to Rs 520 Jefferies retained its ‘Buy’ rating on Kotak Mahindra Bank and raised its target price to Rs 520 from Rs 460. Its October 25 report highlighted healthy loan growth, improving core operating performance and stable asset quality. The bank’s standalone profit after tax rose 29% year on year to Rs 4,212 crore, slightly below Jefferies’ estimate due to higher operating expenses. Net interest income grew 16%, supported by 19% growth in core loans. Jefferies raised its earnings estimates for FY27 to FY29 by 6% to 7%, factoring in stronger core operating trends and the consolidation of KMIL with the standalone bank. The brokerage expects loan growth to compound at 16% over the period and assumes credit costs will normalise towards around 70 basis points of average loans. The brokerage expects stable margins and operating synergies to help offset pressure from lower bancassurance fees. It also noted that Kotak Mahindra Bank’s asset quality remained strong, with a gross non-performing loan ratio of around 1% and a loan coverage ratio of 78%. Jefferies said the bank was valued at 1.5 times its estimated adjusted book value for FY28, compared with 1.9 times for ICICI Bank. It attributed the difference partly to its estimated return on equity of 13% for Kotak Mahindra Bank against 17% for ICICI Bank. docs.title: BSE share price up 4%: Why Motilal Oswal sees 23% upside driven by SEBI VWAP reversal
docs.text: August was a rough month for BSE or the Bombay Stock Exchange. New rules shook up trading, and daily turnover in its futures and options (F&O) segment fell about 35%. Then October arrived, and the numbers jumped back.The domestic brokerage house Motilal Oswal has upgraded BSE to 'Buy' and set a target price of Rs 4,000, implying about 23% upside from current market price. According to the brokerage report dated October 24, the recovery has a reason beyond volatile markets - a rule change coming on December 7. Let’s look at what is driving this investment call - Derivatives volumes bounce back after a regulatory setback BSE’s derivatives business faced pressure after stricter lending norms for proprietary traders came into effect in July 2026, followed by the implementation of the CAS framework in August. These changes reduced trading activity. As per the Motilal Oswal report, BSE’s average daily turnover (ADTO) in futures and options (F&O) fell 35% in August compared with the average between April-July 2026. ALSO READNarayana Murthy’s family office bets Rs 310 cr on 2 new, beaten-down stocks The recovery has since gathered pace. September saw a 6% month-on-month increase, while October recorded a stronger rebound amid volatile market conditions. Motilal Oswal noted that "Oct '26 has seen a significant spurt in volumes, with ADTO up 49% MoM as of 20th Oct’26.” However, the brokerage cautions that market volatility may have contributed to the jump. A sustained recovery, rather than a temporary spike, will be crucial for BSE’s earnings outlook. Will the December regulatory change provide another boost? A further development could support trading activity. The report noted that the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) has partially reversed the CAS changes, restoring the last-30-minute volume-weighted average price (VWAP) settlement mechanism for index derivatives from December 7, 2026. Motilal Oswal expects BSE’s average daily turnover to reach Rs 216 trillion in the FY26-27. This translates to a 16% growth year-on-year. The brokerage also sees scope for higher estimates if the recovery continues. Market share and premium income offer further growth avenues BSE’s growth opportunity extends beyond a rebound in trading volumes. The exchange has already captured more than 30% of the market in premium turnover, which measures the premium value of options traded. The premium-to-notional ratio has increased to around 14 basis points from 6-7 basis points in 2023-24. The ratio remains below the National Stock Exchange’s (NSE) level of more than 20 basis points. ALSO READ ‘Buy’ recommendations by Motilal Oswal with 21% to 34% upside potential Its cash market business is also gaining ground. BSE’s cash market share has increased from around 7% to 9%. Motilal Oswal expects the potential listing of NSE and the opening of its share lock-in period in March 2027 to support trading activity. Can stronger revenues translate into higher profits? BSE is also expanding its revenue streams beyond derivatives trading. Its Star Mutual Fund (Star MF) platform has grown from 12 million quarterly transactions in the first quarter of FY20 to 245 million in the second quarter of FY27. The platform now generates more than Rs 80 crore in quarterly revenue, as per the brokerage report. Co-location services, which allow traders to place their servers close to exchange systems, contribute another Rs 45-48 crore per quarter. BSE’s earnings potential is supported by operating leverage, where revenue growth can translate into faster profit growth as the business expands. Its earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA) margin rose above 65% in FY26 from 9% in FY21. Motilal Oswal expects margins to reach 70% and forecasts a 27% compound annual growth rate (CAGR) in profit after tax between FY26-28. What does the Rs 4,000 target mean for investors? Motilal Oswal has raised its financial estimates and upgraded BSE to ‘Buy’, valuing the stock at 40 times its estimated earnings for FY28. The brokerage sees potential benefits from recovering derivatives volumes, regulatory changes and stronger cash market activity. However, the outlook depends on whether trading volumes remain healthy after the recent volatility-driven rebound. docs.title: Power trading & smart meters: Why Jefferies sees 62% upside in this Adani Group stock
docs.text: Rs 11 crore. That is what one business earned in operating profit a year ago. This time, it earned Rs 800 crore, more than 70 times.The stock in focus is Adani Energy Solutions. Jefferies has retained a 'Buy' rating on the company and set a target price of Rs 1,980, down from its earlier target of Rs 2,060. Even after the revision, the target still implies 62% upside potential from the current market price. Let's take a look at Jefferies outlook on the stock and the reasons behind its bullish call – What changed after the latest results? Adani Energy's earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA) came in 19% higher than Jefferies' expectations, largely because its power trading business performed better than expected. That stronger performance prompted the brokerage to raise its estimate for the FY27 EBITDA by 6%. At the same time, it lowered projections for the FY28 to FY30 by around 4-5%. This is mainly because the management expects lower capital spending in its transmission and smart meter businesses than previously estimated. The report says it remains confident of "25%+ EBITDA CAGR over FY26-30E." ALSO READIndia’s factory boom needs more than factories: 2 stocks, one with 50%+ EBITDA margins Can the trading business become a bigger growth engine? One of the biggest talking points is Adani Energy's power trading business. According to the global investment bank report, "Trading segment EBITDA up 36% QoQ", while its share of overall EBITDA rose to 25% from 20% in the previous quarter. The company has already tied up 4.6 gigawatts of solar and wind power capacity along with 3.5 gigawatt-hours of battery energy storage system capacity. It has also secured a 25-year round-the-clock power supply agreement with Maharashtra State Electricity Distribution. Jefferies estimates that tied-up trading volumes could rise to 57% in FY28E, compared with just 25% in the first quarter of FY27, making earnings from this segment more stable. Adani Energy: What about transmission and smart meters? The transmission business remains another key part of the story. According to the Jefferies report, "Transmission bid pipeline up 45% YoY", reaching Rs 1.4 lakh crore, while projects worth Rs 87,200 crore are currently under execution. However, Jefferies has trimmed its capitalisation estimates for this segment to Rs 9,000-10,000 crore for FY27-28, compared with an earlier estimate of Rs 13,000-15,000 crore, reflecting management's updated guidance. The smart meter business also continues to expand, although at a slower pace. The company has increased its installed base to 1.48 crore smart meters, which is nearly double last year's level. ALSO READBSE share price up 4%: Why Motilal Oswal sees 23% upside driven by SEBI VWAP reversal Some projects in Bihar and Maharashtra have faced delays, leading management to reduce its installation guidance for FY27 to 80-90 lakh meters, instead of the earlier 1 crore target. As per the global investment bank report bidding opportunities still remain large, with 8.6 crore smart meters yet to be awarded under the government's 25 crore-meter programme. Why did Jefferies lower the target price for Adani Energy? Jefferies reduced its target price but did not change its overall view on the stock. According to the report, the revised valuation reflects lower long-term EBITDA estimates after the company updated its capital spending outlook. Jefferies continues to value most of the business at 22 times enterprise value to EBITDA, while assigning a lower multiple to the trading business because its long-term profitability is still evolving. The report also highlighted two key risks. Higher interest costs and any loss of market share could affect future performance. docs.title: Infosys share price slips 3%: Why top brokerages turn cautious after revenue guidance cut
docs.text: The Infosys share price is in focus on Monday, October 26. The IT major announced its earnings for the second quarter of financial year 2027 (Q2FY27) on Friday and also lowered its revenue growth guidance for the year. Most brokerages see limited upside going forward. The stock is down 3% in early trade on Monday. Global investment bank Jefferies has maintained its ‘Hold’ rating and sees a potential downside hereon, while Japanese brokerage Nomura maintained a ‘Buy’ rating with an upside estimate. Nuvama Institutional Equities has downgraded the stock. Infosys Q2FY27 IT giant Infosys lowered its revenue growth guidance for FY27 to 1-2% from 1.5-3% earlier due to pricing pressure on large contracts and weakness in key industry segments. The company retained its operating margin guidance of 20-22%. ALSO READMonday Watchlist: Nifty volatility spikes — IT, Pharma & Realty among key sectors to watch Infosys’ revenue rose 2.1% sequentially to Rs 49,244 crore for Q2FY27, marginally ahead of Bloomberg’s estimate of Rs 49,108 crore. Its net profit increased 0.7% to Rs 7,823 crore, below the estimate of Rs 7,904 crore. Jefferies on Infosys: Lowers target, rates ‘Hold’ The global investment bank Jefferies maintained its ‘Hold’ rating on the stock while lowering its target price to Rs 1,140 from Rs 1,160 earlier. This implies a downside of 1% from the current price of Rs 1,153.80. Jefferies said while strong deal wins were positive, the cut to organic growth guidance surprised negatively. “This (lower FY27 revenue guidance) implies organic revenue growth guidance of -0.7% to 0.4%, a 75bps cut to organic growth at the midpoint. The lower end assumes further macro deterioration, while the upper end assumes improvement,” the bank said. Jefferies lowered its revenue estimates for the company, in dollars, by 1-3% to factor in a weaker second half outlook and expects Infosys to deliver constant currency revenues at 2.6% on a compounded annual growth rate (CAGR) basis over FY27 to FY29. The bank expects margins to be steady at 20.7% over the same period. However, it added that wage hikes and large deal ramp-ups may keep margins under pressure. “With the stock trading at 15x PE/5% dividend yield, we see limited downside, but growth concerns should limit scope for PE re-rating,” it said. Nomura on Infosys: Reduces target price The Japanese brokerage Nomura has maintained its ‘Buy’ rating on the stock, but reduced the target price to Rs 1,300 from Rs 1,310. This implies an upside of nearly 13%. Nomura expects the IT major’s revenue to grow at 1.1-2% in FY27-FY28 from its earlier estimate of 1.2-2.8%. “Infy noted that pricing pressure due to increased competitive intensity, resulting in lower-than-anticipated price increases and softer volume growth in 2QFY27 (below its expectations), led to guidance revision. Management acknowledged that pricing pressure is broad-based across clients due to demands for AI productivity benefits, with some peers being more aggressive, but affirmed that Infosys remains disciplined in pursuing contracts that meet economic return expectations.” Nomura has retained its EBIT margin forecast of 20.8%-21% for FY27-FY28. There could be some headwinds from amortisation for acquisitions, large deal ramp-ups, and AI productivity return to clients. Nuvama on Infosys: Downgrades to ‘Hold’ Brokerage Nuvama has downgraded the stock to ‘Hold’ and has a target price of Rs 1,200. This implies an upside of 4%. The company’s weak performance in the first half of FY27, guidance cut, and likely ramp-down of deals in the second half is likely to lead to a weak FY27 exit rate and hence soft growth in FY28 too. Nuvama believes Infosys is likely to underperform peers, both large-caps and mid-caps, in the near to medium term. “With H2 set to be weaker than it has been historically, the growth outlook stays weak for the near term. Inexpensive valuations limit downside,” it said, adding that margins face wage-hike headwinds phased across Q3 and Q4, pricing and deal ramp-ups headwinds, partly offset by Project Maximus. ALSO READIndian IT stocks rally 12% in a week – Is the turnaround sustainable? Motilal Oswal on Infosys: Underperformance to continue Motilal Oswal has reiterated its ‘Buy’ rating on the stock but has trimmed the FY28 earnings estimates by 1.5% to factor in lower FY27 organic growth guidance and continued pricing pressure from AI-led productivity deflation. While AI revenue continues to scale up, Motilal Oswal believes “productivity pass-through on the existing book of business will remain a near-term headwind. Execution on deal conversion and pricing remains a key monitorable.” Motilal Oswal now has a target of Rs 1,300 per share, implying 13% upside. What investors need to watch out for Most brokerages have put out a cautious view on Infosys after the guidance for FY27 was revised lower. Most see growth pressures continuing, but the deal wins are seen as a key positive going forward. docs.title: Jewellers bet on Dhanteras as buyers lock gold rates amid price volatility
docs.text: With gold prices at elevated levels and the wedding season approaching, jewellers are seeing renewed interest in advance bookings ahead of Dhanteras on November 6. Price-protection schemes, a recent correction in bullion rates and the proximity of the winter wedding season are prompting consumers to plan purchases early rather than wait for the traditional festive rush. The uptick comes after months of cautious spending. Suvankar Sen, MD and CEO of Senco Gold & Diamonds, said pre-orders were on a par with last year, but customer sentiment, footfall and purchase intent had improved over the past three to four months. The company expects festive-season growth of more than 20% over last year. “The Dhanteras market has been positive in terms of value and marginally positive in terms of volume. Pre-orders have been similar to last year. However, with the ongoing auspicious festive season and the upcoming wedding season, we expect consumers to be robust when it comes to purchase of gold and diamond jewellery,” Sen said. ALSO READBeyond Titan and Kalyan: The smallcaps supplying India’s jewellery giants Jewellers are using advance-booking offers to encourage purchases despite volatile bullion prices. “Since we have been running the Pure price offer for Dhanteras and Diwali, pre-bookings are above expectations,” said a senior executive with a top jewellery chain, adding that customers had paid advances and locked in prices. The retailer expects Dhanteras sales to recover some of the shortfall in Dussehra sales. Such offers allow buyers to manage the risk of subsequent price increases, subject to the schemes' terms and conditions. Kalyan Jewellers' rate-protection offer and Joyalukkas' advance-booking option are among the initiatives aimed at consumers concerned about further price volatility. Jewellers are also preparing for redemptions under monthly savings schemes, as customers who have contributed instalments over several months become eligible to use their accumulated amounts towards purchases. 24-carat gold is now trading at around Rs 1.42–1.44 lakh per 10 grams, while silver stood at approximately Rs 1.95–1.96 lakh per kg, according to bullion market sources. The near-term price trajectory remains uncertain. Global instability, central-bank buying and currency movements could support prices, but a further increase by Dhanteras is not guaranteed. Advance bookings offer consumers a way to manage this uncertainty rather than rely on a particular price forecast. Mehul Jain, founder of Ekaraa Jewellery, said consumer sentiment ahead of Dhanteras was encouraging, with preferences extending beyond conventional designs. “Dhanteras continues to hold strong cultural and emotional significance for Indian consumers. Preferences are evolving beyond conventional designs, with growing interest in polki, rose-cut diamonds, coloured diamonds, distinctive diamond cuts and innovative finishes such as ceramic and coloured rhodium,” Jain said. Weddings add to festive demand The calendar is providing jewellers with another demand driver. With a shift in the Diwali season to November, bringing Dhanteras closer to the winter wedding period, retailers are seeing interest in both traditional auspicious purchases, including coins and smaller gold and silver items, and higher-value bridal orders. Yash Kataria, CEO of Kataria Jewellers, expects sales this Dhanteras to grow 35-40% from 2025. Antique and heritage designs in 22-carat gold are witnessing strong demand, while the company's Indore showroom is seeing greater interest in polki and diamond jewellery than its Ratlam outlet in Madhya Pradesh. “There is strong demand for heavy bridal jewellery, particularly for weddings and special occasions, as the preference is for pieces that bring together heritage, versatility and modern sensibilities,” Kataria said. ALSO READTitan’s smaller rivals match its growth—at 41%–85% P/E discounts Higher gold prices are also influencing product choices. Sen expects continued demand for lightweight, everyday-wear jewellery, while old-gold exchanges account for more than 50% of Senco's total business. Exchanges allow customers to use the value of existing jewellery towards new purchases, helping them manage the upfront cost of fresh gold. However, the shift towards smaller, versatile pieces is not universal. Bridal jewellery remains an important category, while design-conscious buyers are seeking distinctive pieces that can be worn beyond the festive season. For affluent consumers, purchases are also becoming less dependent on the festive calendar. Renu Oberoi, founder and creative director of Renu Oberoi, said high-net-worth individuals increasingly buy jewellery throughout the year, guided by personal preferences and spending priorities rather than Dhanteras alone. For retailers, the challenge is to convert advance bookings into sales while catering to households managing affordability and wedding budgets, as well as affluent consumers prioritising design and craftsmanship. Rate protection may bring buyers through the door, but the conversion of bookings, exchange offers, and bridal demand will determine how much festive intent translates into revenue.

docs.title: Narayana Murthy’s family office bets Rs 310 cr on 2 new, beaten-down stocks
docs.text: Narayana Murthy Portfolio: Two New Bets on India's Building Boom Six months ago, the listed portfolio of Narayana Murthy's family office was a short, quiet list. Today it reads like the client roster of an engineering firm. Catamaran Ventures, the investment arm of the Infosys co-founder, has added six manufacturing names to its disclosed holdings in just two quarters. Eight of its nine listed stocks now make something you can touch, from forgings and alloy steel to aircraft parts and generators. The September 2026 shareholding filings add two more. Catamaran now holds 1.06% of Kirloskar Oil Engines, a stake worth about Rs 289 cr, and 1.05% of Ador Welding, worth about Rs 23 cr. That is a fresh commitment of over Rs 310 cr, and the Kirloskar stake alone is now one of the biggest in Catamaran's listed book. FE Stock Insights on WhatsApPGet instant alerts on high-conviction investment themes and fundamental deep dives—direct from Financial Express.Join now Kirloskar Oil Engines now trades about 31% below its 52-week high, Ador Welding about 28%. Both companies have just reported thinner margins, and both blame costlier raw materials. So, is Murthy's office buying a passing dip in two businesses riding India's capex cycle, or stepping into a margin squeeze with further to run? The filings and the financials offer some clues. #1 Kirloskar Oil Engines: The Data Centre Power Stock in Murthy's Book Incorporated in 2009, Kirloskar Oil Engines (KOEL) took over the engine business of the Kirloskar group in a 2010 restructuring. With a market cap of Rs 26,088 cr, it makes generator sets from 1 kW to 10 MW, plus industrial engines for ships, defence, nuclear plants, railways and farms. It claims about 28% of India's generator set market. Catamaran holds 15,43,969 shares. At the closing price of Rs 1,869 on 22nd October 2026, that stake is worth close to Rs 289 cr. Holdings below 1% are not disclosed, so buying may have started earlier. From Farm Pumps to AI Data Centres: The 192 MW HyperNext Order Much of the rally rests on data centres. A data centre cannot go dark when the grid trips, so every server hall needs backup generators, and the big ones need dozens. On 19th June 2026, KOEL told the BSE it had won an order from HyperNext, a data centre developer, for 96 units of its 2,500 kVA Optiprime power systems, adding up to 192 MW. The company called it one of India's largest standby power deployments for data centres. The stock hit its 20% upper circuit on the next trading day. Management now wants KOEL to become a USD 2 billion revenue company by FY30, a little over twice its FY26 consolidated sales. The board has cleared Rs 2,100 cr of new capacity at its Kagal plant, of which Rs 1,400 cr is meant for large engines aimed at data centres and exports. Kirloskar Oil Engines Financials: 30% EBITDA Growth, With a Lender Inside A caution first. KOEL's consolidated accounts include Arka Fincap, its lending arm. That is why consolidated borrowings stood at Rs 5,374 cr in FY26, while the engine business on its own carried just Rs 131 cr. Of the Rs 523 cr of consolidated interest cost, only Rs 11 cr sits in the standalone business. Financial YearFY21FY22FY23FY24FY25FY265Y CAGRSales (Rs cr)3,2964,0225,0205,8986,3297,70118%EBITDA (Rs cr)3874127341,0271,1811,41430%Net Profit (Rs cr)19717133244047656223% Source: Screener.in EBITDA here refers to operating profit before other income. Since Arka's interest cost sits below the EBITDA line, that 30% flatters the factory. The standalone engine business grew sales at 16% a year from FY21 to FY26, operating profit at 21% and net profit at 22%. ALSO READ4x oil production target by FY30: An under-the-radar smallcap betting on bigger profits The latest quarter is where the worry sits. In Q1 FY27, standalone sales rose 16% to Rs 1,461 cr, but EBITDA fell 4% and the margin slipped to 11.2% from 13.5%. Management blamed weaker exports, higher commodity costs and a delay in passing on price hikes. Consolidated profit fell 17% to Rs 111 cr. Kirloskar Oil Engines Share Price: A 3x Swing in 12 Months The share price of Kirloskar Oil Engines has compounded at 53% a year over five years, as per Screener. In the past 12 months it went from a low of Rs 883 to a high of Rs 2,720, a little over three times, before closing at Rs 1,869 on 22nd October 2026. After the fall, it still trades at a PE of about 46x against a current industry median of about 38x, and at 7 times book value. The 10-year median PE for the company is 23x while the industry median for the same period is 34x. Its larger rival, Cummins India, trades at about 49x. Promoters hold 41.03%, domestic institutions 27.04% and foreign investors 11.06%. Retail has piled in too. The number of shareholders rose from 68,891 in December 2023 to 1,28,854 in September 2026. Margin Squeeze and the Rs 2,100 Crore Kagal Bet: What Could Go Wrong Three things need watching. Margins, because another quarter near 11% would test a 46x multiple, and Q2 FY27 numbers are due in the coming weeks. Execution, because Rs 2,100 cr of capex is a big cheque for a business that earned Rs 461 cr of standalone profit in FY26. And competition, because in data centre gensets KOEL is the challenger, not the incumbent, and big orders tend to be lumpy. #2 Ador Welding: A 75-Year-Old Welding Stock at 18x Earnings Incorporated in 1951, Ador Welding is one of India's oldest welding companies. With a market cap of Rs 2,211 cr, it makes welding electrodes, wires, fluxes, machines and automation systems from five plants, with capacity for 90,000 tonnes of consumables and 30,000 welding machines a year. Catamaran holds 1,82,798 shares, or 1.05%, worth about Rs 23 cr at Rs 1,270. That is a starter-sized position, roughly one-twelfth of what it has put into Kirloskar Oil Engines. Why Every Bridge, Pipeline and Factory Needs a Welder Almost everything India is building, from bridges and pipelines to ships, power plants and factory sheds, is held together by a weld.

docs.title: Infosys vs TCS: Which IT stock offers better value after Q2? Deal wins, AI growth in focus
docs.text: Infosys and Tata Consultancy Services (TCS) reported modest revenue growth in the September 2026 quarter, as clients remained cautious about technology spending and demand varied across industries and geographies. Most brokerages are cautious and see room for limited upside in the near-term. Both companies reported progress in artificial intelligence (AI), while their quarterly results showed that new technology work and large contracts have yet to translate into a broad acceleration in revenue. ALSO READIndia’s factory boom needs more than factories: 2 stocks, one with 50%+ EBITDA margins Infosys reported large-deal total contract value (TCV) of $5.2 billion, while TCS recorded deal bookings of $9.6 billion. Infosys also lowered its FY27 revenue growth guidance, whereas TCS reported an operating margin of 24.0% and annualised AI revenue of $3.1 billion. The two companies face different challenges: Infosys must convert its large-deal pipeline into revenue after cutting guidance, while TCS must sustain growth and manage costs that could pressure its margins. Infosys vs TCS: Revenue growth remains modest Infosys reported revenue of $5.145 billion in Q2FY27, up 1.2% sequentially and 1.5% year-on-year in constant-currency terms. Revenue in reported currency rose 1.3% year on year. Operating profit increased 1.3% year-on-year to $1.079 billion, while operating margin stood at 21.0%, compared with 21.1% in the June quarter. Net profit declined 2.5% year on year to $817 million. ALSO READBrokerage consensus stocks: Swiggy, Eternal among 6 stock picks with 22% to 91% upside The company’s operating margin remained at 21%, while its revised annual growth guidance indicated that demand had not improved enough to support its previous outlook. Infosys Chief Executive Officer and Managing Director Salil Parekh said, “We are advising some of the largest global enterprises on their AI strategy and continue to invest in deep domain and technology capabilities to bring new ideas and an integrated ecosystem to help businesses unlock AI value at scale.” Global investment bank Jefferies believes “Infosys' soft growth outlook should also keep margins in check.” TCS reported revenue of $7.642 billion, up 0.5% sequentially in constant-currency terms and 2.8% year on year on the same basis. Revenue in reported currency increased 2.4% year on year to Rs 73,187 crore. Operating margin was 24.0%, unchanged sequentially but below 25.2% a year earlier. TCS reported net profit of $1.45 billion, equivalent to Rs 13,075 crore, for the quarter. TCS Chief Financial Officer Samir Seksaria said, “Our operating margins remained stable sequentially at 24%.” He also said, "Annualised AI revenue reached $3.1 billion and crossed 10% of our overall revenue.” The comments were made during TCS’s October 8 earnings call. While the company maintained its sequential operating margin, the year-on-year comparison showed a decline, and Jefferies identified higher subcontracting costs and overheads as areas of concern. It retained its operating margin guidance of 20%-22%. The company’s revised outlook reflected a weaker-than-expected first half, with softer volumes and lower-than-anticipated price increases affecting revenue growth. Jefferies estimated that the revised range implied organic revenue growth of between -0.7% and 0.4% for FY27, with a 75-basis-point reduction at the midpoint compared with the earlier guidance. The brokerage cut its revenue estimates and expects organic constant-currency revenue to grow at a compound annual growth rate of 2.3% over FY27-FY29. TCS does not provide specific revenue or earnings guidance, as noted at the start of its earnings call. Its September-quarter results nevertheless showed uneven demand across geographies. International operations grew 1.2% sequentially in constant-currency terms, while India operations declined 10.0%, which Jefferies attributed to project deferrals. The UK grew 3.5% sequentially, providing support against weaker performance in other markets. The difference is that Infosys has formally lowered its annual growth range, while TCS’ outlook must be assessed through its quarterly performance, management commentary and contract pipeline. Infosys faces the task of delivering growth within its revised range. Neither company’s results point to a rapid, broad-based recovery in client spending. Infosys vs TCS: Large deals provide support, but conversion matters Infosys reported large-deal TCV of $5.2 billion for the September quarter, up 70% year-on-year. The company said 62% of its large-deal TCV was net new. Its wins included a seven-year financial-services deal worth more than $2 billion in net-new business, expected to begin ramping up in the fourth quarter, and a separate $1 billion renewal. Parekh described the large-deal pipeline as healthy during the earnings call. The company expects the $2 billion-plus contract to contribute more than 1% to revenue growth in the coming financial year. That contribution will depend on the pace at which the contract ramps up and the work is recognised as revenue.TCS reported quarterly deal bookings of $9.6 billion. Its results release identified strategic deals involving Porsche and Best Buy. Jefferies said bookings were down 4% year on year when excluding the Porsche and Best Buy deals from the comparison. The brokerage also identified the second phase of TCS’s BSNL engagement as a potential source of support for revenue growt

docs.title: 7x earnings, a 59% fall: Vijay Kedia and Dolly Khanna’s latest smallcap bets
docs.text: Vijay Kedia and Dolly Khanna Go Shopping in the Smallcap Bargain Bin Shareholding data for the September 2026 quarter shows two familiar names going against the market's mood. Vijay Kedia, through his firm Kedia Securities, took a fresh 1.49% stake in Zaggle Prepaid Ocean Services. The fintech stock has lost nearly 59% of its value in a year. Dolly Khanna made a quieter move. She is back in Rajshree Polypack, a maker of plastic food packaging, with 1.05%. She had dropped off its shareholder list after March 2025. The stock trades below its book value. On the surface, a software-led payments firm and a plastic cup maker have little in common. But both have been marked down hard, both grew sales at over 20% a year for five years, and both now trade at a lower PE than the median for their industry. The question is whether the market has priced in too much bad news, or not enough. FE Stock Insights on WhatsApPGet instant alerts on high-conviction investment themes and fundamental deep dives—direct from Financial Express.Join now #1 Zaggle’s 59% Wipeout: Why Kedia Replaced Kacholia in the September Quarter Zaggle Prepaid Ocean Services helps companies manage what their staff spend. It issues prepaid and corporate cards, and runs software for expense claims, vendor payments and employee rewards. As of FY26, it served 3,915 corporate customers and about 39 lakh users. It came to the market in September 2023 at an IPO price of Rs 164. The timing of Kedia's entry is the story. On 17th August 2026, the stock fell 20% after its June quarter profit dropped 33%. On the same day, the company disclosed that its appeal against an income tax demand for AY 2022-23 had been dismissed. The next day, according to bulk deal data on the exchange, Kedia Securities bought 20 lakh shares at Rs 164.72, almost exactly the IPO price, for about Rs 33 cr. These aren’t the first small cap names added to Kedia’s portfolio recently, Recently, I also wrote about 2 more small cap stocks Vijay Kedia invested in, which you must read about. Then came the twist. Ashish Kacholia had held 2.16% of Zaggle in June 2026. In the September filing, his name is missing. Individual holders are named in these filings only once they own 1% or more, so his stake has at least shrunk under that mark. Whether he sold everything is unknown. What is clear is that one well-known smallcap investor reduced his position in the same quarter another chose to buy. Five Years of 50% Sales Growth, But Thinner Margins The long-term growth record is hard to fault. Sales have grown nearly eight-fold in five years, and profit has grown about seven-fold. The catch is in the margins. Operating margin was 16% in FY22. It has sat at 9 to 10% since. Zaggle earns more as it grows, but it keeps a smaller slice of each rupee. ALSO READVijay Kedia’s latest bets: Rs 73 cr in 2 smallcaps with surging profits The June 2026 quarter made that worse. Sales rose 18% from a year earlier, but net profit fell from Rs 26 cr to Rs 17 cr, and margin slipped to 7%. Management attributed the drop to approximately Rs 3 crore in integration costs for DICE, a newly acquired expense software business—noting that related revenue is only expected to reflect from the September quarter onwards. The deal itself was reworked into an asset purchase for Rs 68 cr, down from Rs 123 cr earlier. Management also kept its FY27 target of about 40% revenue growth. Zaggle is also looking abroad. On 22nd October 2026, it set up a wholly owned subsidiary in the Abu Dhabi Global Market, with a starting capital of USD 10,000. It is a small first step, but it points to Gulf ambitions. The FCF Reality: Profit vs. Cash Conversion The share price of Zaggle was around Rs 158 on its listing day in September 2023 and as of closing on 26th October 2026 it was Rs 152. That is below the IPO price, 73% below its January 2025 peak, and about 9% under what Kedia paid. On valuations, the stock trades at a PE of 17x compared to the current industry median of 20x. Its median PE since listing in 2023 is 65x, while the 10-year industry median is 31x. The stock has gone from one of the priciest names in its group to one of the cheaper ones. Smart money has been leaving. Domestic institutions held 14.56% in December 2024 and just 2.69% by September 2026. Foreign investors fell from 9.17% to 2.49% over the same period. Small shareholders filled the gap. Their number rose 42% to about 1.29 lakh. One more figure deserves attention: free cash flow was negative Rs 113 cr in FY26, so the profits are not yet turning into cash. #2 Rajshree Polypack: Dolly Khanna Returns to a Packaging Stock at 7x Earnings Incorporated in 2011, Rajshree Polypack makes the plastic cups, tubs, lids and sheets that hold your curd, ice cream and takeaway food. Its products also include printed sleeves and moulded parts. Dairy, quick-service restaurants and online food delivery are among the end markets management says are growing. It also runs a paper-based food packaging joint venture, Olive Ecopak. Dolly Khanna has been here before. She held 1.16% in December 2024 and 1.08% in March 2025, then vanished from the list for five quarters. She also returned to Rain Industries in the same quarter, a sign she is revisiting old names rather than chasing new ones. The September 2026 filing shows her back with 7.78 lakh shares, or 1.05%. At the current price, that is worth only about Rs 1.4 cr, a small bet even in her Rs 323 cr portfolio. This addition comes after the brutal clean up Dolly Khanna did in the last quarter. docs.title: 15-fold dividend jump, 3.2% yield: A shipping PSU for your 2027 watchlist
docs.text: Welcome to the latest edition of Dividend Hunter. In recent weeks, we have analysed companies where strong cash flows could translate into consistent dividends. In our previous edition, we covered a diversified public sector company that delivered a 3.5% dividend yield. This week, in our Dividend Hunter series, we discuss a Navratna central public sector enterprise. The company is India’s largest shipping enterprise, operating a diverse fleet of 58 owned vessels across crude & product tankers, bulk carriers, container liners, offshore support, and gas transport (LPG/LNG). During the last five financial years, its standalone revenue and net profit grew at a CAGR of 9% and 16% respectively. Over the same period, its share price returned 18% CAGR. In fact, its consolidated net profit grew faster by 62.9% year-on-year to ₹1,326 crore in FY26. For FY26, the company returned 26.3% of Net Profit to shareholders as dividend distributions. Moreover, during the FY24-26 period, its dividend per share (DPS) increased from ₹0.50 to ₹7.50, a 15-fold rise. During this period, the company's total dividend payout increased from ₹23.3 crore to ₹349.4 crore. This surge in payouts occurred as the company nearly doubled its net profit to ₹1,326 crore in FY26. FE Stock Insights on WhatsApPGet instant alerts on high-conviction investment themes and fundamental deep dives—direct from Financial Express.Join now The company is Shipping Corporation of India (SCI). Shipping Corporation of India Share Price From ₹0.50 to ₹7.50: How DIPAM Net Worth Rules Unlocked SCI’s 15-Fold Dividend Surge SCI paid a per-share dividend of ₹7.5 in FY26, translating into a dividend yield of 3.2% at the current price (as of October 23) of ₹238. During the year, the company paid two interim dividends totalling ₹6.5 and a final dividend of ₹1.0 per share. Typically, the company pays a dividend every year in September and November. One common pattern is the sharp increase in dividend payouts over the past two years. Between FY22 and FY24, the company distributed just ₹15.4 crore to ₹23.3 crore annually, with its dividend payout ratio remaining below 4%. This changed significantly in FY25, when the dividend per share jumped to ₹6.59 and the total payout rose to ₹307 crore, accounting for 37.7% of net profit. In FY26, the company further increased the dividend per share to ₹7.5, taking the total payout to ₹349.4 crore. However, with net profit rising to ₹1,326 crore, the payout ratio moderated to 26.3%. This indicates that the company has stepped up shareholder returns while retaining a larger share of its earnings to support future growth. The tanker division was the primary driver of growth during the year. Tanker revenue increased by 9.2% year-on-year to ₹3,942.2 crore, while the segment’s profit rose by 74.9% to ₹1,189.5 crore. ALSO READRs 2.35 lakh cr naval push: 2 stocks to watch as India targets 200 warships Profitability was driven by higher freight rates, more time-charter days, and active spot market deployment. Growth was also supported by increased overall tonne-mile demand due to the longer trade route and the Strait of Hormuz blockade. Bulk carrier revenue increased 10.9% year-on-year to ₹788.9 crore, while losses narrowed to ₹19.1 crore from ₹22.2 crore. Revenue improved due to higher voyage charters and better fleet deployment, supported by a 74% higher Baltic Dry Index in the fourth quarter. Revenue from the liner segment declined to ₹784 crore from ₹1,036 crore in the previous year, while segment profit fell to ₹74.84 crore. Lower container freight rates and reduced cargo volumes weighed on the segment’s performance. However, coastal liner services continued to maintain high vessel utilisation, providing some support amid weaker market conditions. Technical and Offshore Support contributed ₹297.9 crore to revenue in FY26. Other income stood at ₹440.2 crore, providing additional support to the overall financial performance. EBITDA (Earnings Before Interest, Tax, Depreciation, and Amortisation) grew faster by 45.6% to ₹2,632.9 crore during the year, while margin expanded by 10.5 percentage points to 45.6%. Lower operating expenses (-10.8%), a shift in revenue-mix towards the higher-margin tanker business, an increase in other income (+128%) and a reduction in bulk carrier losses helped improve margins. This operational leverage pushed Standalone net profit up 62.9% to ₹1,326 crore. SCI returned 26.3% of this net profit to shareholders as dividends. In addition to the year's standalone net profit, the Board evaluates retained earnings, projected cash flows, working capital requirements, debt maturity profile, capex freight and charter hire rates, and debt servicing agreements before declaring a dividend. Higher Freight Rates Acting as a Tailwind For instance, during FY26, higher time-charter rates and spot freight rate spikes during Middle East trade disruptions boosted the company profitability. This prompted the board to deliver higher dividend per share and total payout even though the payout ratio declined. For FY27, the outlook also remains favourable for tanker operators. Freight rates are still higher supported by ongoing geopolitical disruptions, longer shipping routes and tight effective vessel availability. docs.title: Average balance in PMJDY accounts touches a record Rs 5,438
docs.text: The average balance in no-frills bank accounts under the Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY) has hit a new high of Rs 5,438 after fresh accretion of around Rs 7,000 crore in less than two months. These accounts now hold cumulative deposits of around Rs 3.24 lakh crore as of October 14, up from Rs 3.17 lakh crore on August 19, 2026. As a result, the average balance rose from Rs 5,356 to a new record of Rs 5,438. The average deposit has risen consistently — from Rs 3,449 in March 2021. ALSO READKarnataka, Keralam, Assam report strong capex in H1 The number of PMJDY accounts has also grown, reaching 595.9 million, up from 590.9 million about two months back. Public sector banks continue to dominate the scheme, accounting for nearly 77% of beneficiaries and deposits. Public sector banks had 458.4 million beneficiaries and deposits of Rs 2.52 lakh crore. Regional rural banks (RRBs) accounted for another 111.8 million beneficiaries, with deposits of Rs 61,311 crore. Private sector banks had 23.8 million beneficiaries and deposits of Rs 10,265 crore, while rural cooperative banks accounted for 1.9 million beneficiaries. The distribution of accounts underscores the importance of rural banking infrastructure in expanding access to formal financial services. Of the total beneficiaries, 462.7 million were associated with rural and semi-urban bank branches, compared with 133.2 million at urban and metropolitan branches. Rural and semi-urban beneficiaries thus accounted for around 78% of the total, reflecting the scheme’s focus on extending banking access beyond major urban centres. Women accounted for 332.3 million beneficiaries, or nearly 56% of the total. This points to the scheme’s role in expanding women’s access to formal banking and strengthening their participation in the financial system. Banks had issued 417.9 million RuPay debit cards to beneficiaries, equivalent to around 70% of the total beneficiary base. The gap between beneficiary numbers and cards issued indicates scope to deepen the use of digital payment facilities and formal banking services. ALSO READOctober PMI rises to 56.7; Input cost inflation eased, manufacturing strong The trinity of Jan Dhan, Aadhaar and mobile (JAM) has played a key role in enabling large-scale, technology-driven, real-time direct benefit transfers (DBTs), especially during the Covid-19 pandemic. Between FY15 and FY24, direct benefit transfers have generated cumulative savings of nearly Rs 5.14 lakh crore. PMJDY accounts require no minimum balance and offer interest on deposits, making them both accessible and appealing for low-income households. These accounts are eligible for direct benefit transfer (DBT), Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana, Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana, Atal Pension Yojana, and Micro Units Development & Refinance Agency Bank (MUDRA) scheme.

docs.title: Why this week could test Wall Street even if the Fed stays quiet
docs.text: Wall Street is heading into a crucial week. Global investors will be glued to some major events, including the Federal Reserve’s interest-rate decision, earnings from major technology companies and fresh US economic data. Markets are also watching whether concerns over artificial intelligence (AI) spending, rising oil prices and persistent inflation will continue to weigh on stocks. So what could tip the balance? All these events are likely to influence investor sentiment. Will Warsh Drop Any Hints on Rates This Week? The Federal Open Market Committee’s two-day meeting begins on October 27. Fed Chair Kevin Warsh will announce the policy decision on October 28. Investors will look for clues on the interest-rate outlook, particularly as inflation remains elevated and concerns about economic growth persist. Do not expect Warsh to reveal much, though. He has often said that inflation remains the priority, but decisions will be based on incoming data. Warsh is not in favour of providing forward guidance, so markets remain unsure about the Fed’s next move. The futures market expects rates to remain unchanged in October with over 90% probability, but forecasts a 25bps rate hike in December, with 70% chances. Key events to watch on Wall Street this week DateEventWhat investors will watch10/27/26US consumer confidence and durable goods ordersConsumer sentiment, business demand and economic strengthOctober 27–28Federal Reserve policy meetingInterest-rate decision and signals on future rate moves10/28/26Fed policy decisionInflation outlook and clues on a possible December rate hike10/28/26Microsoft and Alphabet earningsAI spending, data-centre investments and returns10/29/26Amazon and Intel earningsCloud growth, AI demand and semiconductor outlook10/29/26US Q3 GDP and September PCE inflation dataEconomic growth and inflation pressuresOctober 29–30Bank of Japan policy meetingInterest rates and Japan's inflation outlook10/28/26Bank of Canada policy decisionInterest-rate outlook and economic conditions10/29/26European Central Bank policy decisionInflation, growth and borrowing costs10/31/26Exxon Mobil and Chevron earningsOil prices, energy demand and earnings outlook Three More Central Banks Join the Action The Fed is not the only one deciding. The Bank of Canada also announces its decision on Wednesday. The ECB follows on Thursday. Then comes Japan. The BOJ meets October 29 to 30 and is reportedly leaning toward leaving rates unchanged, even though Japan’s core inflation rose to 2.1% in September from 1.7% in August. That is the first reading above the BOJ’s 2% target since December 2025. The pressure to act is building. Globally, inflation remains in focus and therefore how some of the world's major central banks use monetary policy tool to tame it remains to be seen. Big Tech Earnings Put AI Spending on Trial The earnings calendar is another major focus. Microsoft, Alphabet and Amazon are among the companies scheduled to report results this week. Their earnings and comments on AI investments could help investors judge whether the enormous spending on data centres and computing infrastructure is turning into sustainable business growth. According to market experts, concerns about AI investment, financing needs and potential returns have become important drivers of stock market sentiment. The reaction to the results could matter as much as the numbers. Over 40% of S&P 500 companies report this week, including some mega-cap tech companies. Boeing, Coca-Cola, UPS, PayPal and Visa report on Tuesday. Microsoft and Alphabet report on Wednesday after the market close. Amazon and Intel follow on Thursday. Exxon Mobil and Chevron close out the week on Friday. ALSO READGold nears $4,000: 7 global triggers driving prices that investors cannot ignore How Wall Street Ended a Choppy Week US stock markets ended last week mixed as investors reassessed AI spending, inflation pressures and the outlook for interest rates. Technology stocks came under pressure, while small-cap and value stocks outperformed. That points to a shift away from some of the market’s biggest growth names. The Nasdaq Composite fell 0.71% for the week, while the S&P 500 declined 0.47%. The Dow Jones Industrial Average gained 0.41%, and the Russell 2000 index of small-cap stocks rose 2%. Meta was among the notable decliners as investors focused on its capital spending plans and potential financing needs. Meta and Netflix both fell more than 5% after earnings, dragging communication services down over 5%. So, what is weighing on tech stocks? The pressure intensified towards the end of the week. Investors questioned whether heavy investments in AI infrastructure, including data centres and computing capacity, would generate enough returns to justify the spending. Concerns over funding needs and elevated valuations also weighed on semiconductor and other AI-related stocks. ALSO READUS banking stocks fall up to 25% in 3 months, is a bigger crisis brewing? Why Did Bond Yields Fall Despite Inflation Worries? Expectations of higher-for-longer interest rates still prevail. Even so, investors rushed to buy bonds, pulling yields lower. Treasury yields dropped sharply as tech sold off and geopolitical worries grew. The 10-year yield slipped below 5% for the first time in about a month and settled near 4.99% on Friday. It remains at the same level on Monday. Oil Climbs Above $116 While Gold Slips 4% Oil went the other way, trading above $116 a barrel, while gold fell 4% on the week to around $4,010. Oil and gold continue to trade around the same levels on Monday. Oil returned to focus as renewed tensions in the Middle East raised concerns about energy supplies. Higher oil prices could put further pressure on inflation, complicating the Fed’s task of bringing price growth under control. docs.title: WPL 2027 Auction: Team-wise purse, remaining slots and players needed
docs.text: The countdown to the Women's Premier League (WPL) 2027 auction has begun, with all five franchises preparing to fill the remaining gaps in their squads ahead of the tournament's fifth edition. The auction will be held at the Grand Hyatt Kochi on October 28, starting at 5:30 PM IST. The upcoming season is scheduled to run from January 14 to February 7, 2027. A total of 146 players have been shortlisted for the mini-auction, with 27 slots available across the five teams. These include 20 positions for Indian players and seven for overseas recruits. With limited vacancies and varying budgets, each franchise will have to balance its squad requirements against its remaining purse. UP Warriorz have the most slots to fill and the largest reported budget, while Gujarat Giants have the fewest vacancies. ALSO READWPL 2027 Auction: Date, time, player list, teams, rules – All you need to know WPL 2027 auction: Team-wise remaining purse and slots TeamRemaining purseAvailable slotsOverseas slotsUP Warriorz₹3.75 crore83Gujarat Giants₹1.25 crore31Royal Challengers Bengaluru₹1.15 crore52Delhi Capitals₹1.10 crore51Mumbai Indians₹90 lakh60Total₹8.15 crore277 UP Warriorz: Biggest purse, most slots to fill UP Warriorz will enter the auction with a reported remaining purse of ₹3.75 crore and eight slots to fill, including three overseas positions. They have the greatest financial flexibility among the five franchises. The team will need to use its budget strategically to strengthen its squad across multiple departments. With several positions available, UP Warriorz could target a combination of experienced overseas players and promising Indian talent. Their three overseas slots could be particularly important in shaping the balance of the squad for the upcoming season. Gujarat Giants: Three vacancies, ₹1.25 crore available Gujarat Giants have three slots to fill, including one overseas position, with a reported purse of ₹1.25 crore. With fewer vacancies than most of their rivals, the franchise can focus on specific squad requirements rather than making extensive changes. Its auction strategy will depend on whether it prioritises an experienced overseas recruit or invests in emerging Indian players. Royal Challengers Bengaluru: Five slots, two overseas positions Defending champions Royal Challengers Bengaluru (RCB) have five available slots and a reported remaining purse of ₹1.15 crore. Two of their vacancies are reserved for overseas players. RCB will look to maintain the balance that helped them win the previous edition while addressing any gaps in their squad. Their overseas recruitment will be an important part of the auction strategy, alongside opportunities to add depth to the Indian contingent. Delhi Capitals: Five slots with ₹1.10 crore remaining Delhi Capitals have five vacancies to fill, including one overseas position, with a reported purse of ₹1.10 crore. The franchise will need to identify players who can complement its retained core while providing additional options across batting, bowling and all-rounder roles. With a relatively limited budget compared with UP Warriorz, Delhi Capitals will have to prioritise their requirements carefully. Mumbai Indians: Six vacancies, lowest remaining purse Mumbai Indians have six slots available but the smallest reported remaining purse at ₹90 lakh. The team has no overseas slots left to fill, according to the supplied figures. That leaves Mumbai Indians with a focus on strengthening their Indian contingent. The franchise will need to make its remaining funds count, targeting players who can add depth and provide cover for its retained squad. ALSO READCristiano Ronaldo fined $285: How much does he pocket every 30 seconds? WPL 2027 auction: What each team needs The number of vacancies and overseas slots provides a snapshot of the challenges facing each franchise at the auction. TeamMain auction priorityUP WarriorzFill eight vacancies while maximising the largest remaining purseGujarat GiantsAddress three specific squad gaps, including one overseas positionRoyal Challengers BengaluruStrengthen the squad with two overseas recruits and Indian optionsDelhi CapitalsAdd depth across key roles within the available budgetMumbai IndiansStrengthen the Indian contingent with six vacancies and limited funds WPL 2027 auction: Date, time and where to watch live The WPL 2027 mini-auction is scheduled for October 28 at the Grand Hyatt Kochi, with proceedings beginning at 5:30 PM IST. Television coverage will be on Star Sports channels, while online streaming will be available on JioHotstar. With 27 slots to be filled across five teams, the auction will be a key opportunity for franchises to complete their squads ahead of the WPL 2027 season, scheduled to begin on January 14.

docs.text:
Buy Kotak Mahindra Bank; target of Rs 500: Motilal Oswal
 KOTAKBANK 
 Motilal Oswal's research report on Kotak Mahindra Bank 
 Kotak Mahindra Bank (KMB) posted a standalone 2QFY27 PAT of INR42.1b (in line; up 29% YoY/2% QoQ), aided by healthy NII growth, partly offset by high provisioning. Consol PAT stood at INR56.4b (up 26% YoY/3% QoQ). NII grew 16% YoY/7% QoQ to INR84.6b (in line). NIMs declined 22bp QoQ to 4.31% (below est. of 4.43%), largely on account of strong FCNR (B) sourcing. Advances grew 25% YoY/13% QoQ to INR5.8t. Excl. FCNR (B) related and KMIL loans, growth was 19% YoY/8% QoQ, aided by growth in SME and corporate banking and some pickup in unsecured segments. 
 Outlook 
 We upgrade our earnings estimates by 3%/7% for FY27/28E and estimate RoA/RoE of 2.07%/12.5% by FY27. Reiterate BUY with a revised TP of INR500 (2.0x Mar’28E ABV + SoTP of INR155). Buy Kotak Mahindra Bank: target of Rs 520: ICICI Securities
 KOTAKBANK 
 ICICI Securities research report on Kotak Mahindra Bank 
 Kotak Mahindra Bank (KMB) reported Q2FY27 PAT of INR 42.1bn (up 29% YoY; 4% miss), led by 21% PPOP growth, while slippages/credit costs eased further. Most retail products saw healthy growth of 4–5% QoQ. NII grew 7% QoQ, though adj. for KMIL seems ~5%. NIM, however, dipped 23bps QoQ to 4.31%, mainly on FCNR and adverse day counts. KMB has garnered huge FCNR deposits of INR 553bn (10% of Q1FY27 deposits; ~30% levered), which, in our view, addresses tenure longevity and also improves growth visibility. We expect KMB to remain fastest growing (FY26-28E loan CAGR of 22%) with superior RoA (>2%) within our coverage. 
 Outlook 
 Maintain BUY with a revised TP of INR 520 (vs. INR 480), basis ~2.2x FY28E banking business (2x earlier). Buy Kotak Mahindra Bank; target of Rs 510: Prabhudas Lilladher
 KOTAKBANK 
 Prabhudas Lilladher's research report on Kotak Mahindra Bank 
 KMB saw a good quarter with a beat on all core metrics. While reported NIM was down 22bps QoQ to 4.3% due to FCNR and day count, margins may have bottomed out given Q3FY27 would see impact of (1) FCNR deposits being deployed into assets and (2) repo rate transmission. Adjusted for FCNR/KMIL, loan growth was strong at 7.8% QoQ and 19% YoY. Unsecured loan accretion, that slowed down over Q2FY25 to Q2FY26, has been consistently growing, given moderation in stress; this is likely to sustain. While we raise loan growth by 100bps in FY28 to 16% YoY, there are upside risks to loan growth and NIM as unsecured growth has bounced back. 
 Outlook 
 We maintain multiple at 2.0x on Sep’28 core ABV but raise TP to INR510 from INR500. Retain ‘BUY’. docs.title: BSE shares jump over 4% as Motilal Oswal upgrades stock to Buy. 4 reasons behind bullish call
docs.text:
Shares of BSE rallied as much as 4.3% to their day’s high of Rs 3,369 on the BSE on Monday after Motilal Oswal upgraded the stock to Buy and assigned a target price of Rs 4,000, an upside of 23%.
 BSE’s scalable business model allows incremental revenue to translate into healthy profit growth. Its EBITDA margin rose sharply to over 65% in FY26 from 9% in FY21, reflecting strong operating leverage, the brokerage said.
With margins projected to expand further to 70%, PAT is expected to grow at a CAGR of around 27% over FY26-28, against a revenue CAGR of 23%. Regulatory costs, which account for 55% of operating expenses and are variable in nature, also offer some protection against a slowdown in trading volumes.
 1.) Strong growth path - Since BSE relaunched derivatives in 2023, the impact of most regulatory changes, including F&O 2.0 and the shift in weekly expiry day, has been temporary. BSE achieved around 50% market share in index options notional turnover within three years of the relaunch, while volumes continued to show strong momentum.
However, recent regulatory changes, including stricter lending norms for proprietary traders effective July 2026 and CAS implementation in August 2026, led to a reset in the volume base. BSE’s notional F&O average daily traded turnover (ADTO) fell 35% in August 2026 compared with the April-July 2026 average.
 Live Events
Following the reset, September 2026 saw a modest recovery, with ADTO rising 6% month-on-month. Volumes picked up significantly in October amid volatile markets, with ADTO up 49% month-on-month as of October 20, 2026.
 2.) Premium turnover has more strength - Premium turnover, which contributes 60% of BSE’s revenue, has reached a market share of over 30%, indicating further room for growth given BSE’s around 50% share in notional turnover.
 Also read: Nifty's PEG ratio near 10-year low but why don't stocks look cheap yet? Valuation paradox explained 
The P/N ratio has improved significantly from 6-7 bps in 2023-24 to 8-11 bps in 2025 and around 14 bps currently, reflecting a growing trend towards trading longer-term contracts. However, it remains below NSE’s ratio of over 20 bps.
Factors that could drive BSE’s P/N ratio higher include wider institutional participation supported by colocation expansion, an increase in higher-premium longer-dated expiry contracts to reduce the concentration of volumes on expiry days, and new products offering more monthly expiry contracts. Higher-premium stock options could also gain traction, given their P/N ratio of 120-150 bps on NSE, once NSE enters the F&O segment.
 3.) Beyond derivatives - BSE’s cash market share has risen from a plateau of around 7% to 9% over the past two months, with cash average daily traded turnover (ADTO) reaching a new quarterly high of Rs 105 billion in Q2FY27. The growth was supported by the introduction of a single contract note, implementation of smart order routing and the exclusive listing of popular stocks such as NSE and NSDL.
The number of cash market members increased to 829 in September 2026 from 806 a year earlier, while the number of unique client codes (UCCs) traded hit a record 6.16 million during the month, reflecting rising participation on the platform.
Cash market volumes are expected to grow further, driven by wider adoption of smart order routing and a ramp-up in NSE’s ADTO following the expiry of its lock-in period in March 2027.
 4.) Robust margin ahead - BSE’s EBITDA margin expanded from 9% in FY21 to over 65% in FY26, driven by a 57% revenue CAGR over FY21-26.
Around 45% of its expenses are fixed, while the remaining 55% are activity-dependent. These include clearing house expenses, which vary with the number of derivative contracts, and regulatory costs, which are linked to derivatives notional turnover.
While a slowdown in volumes could weigh on revenue growth, the impact on profitability should be partly offset by lower clearing house and regulatory expenses.
The brokerage expects EBITDA margins to reach 70%, supported by a 23% revenue CAGR over FY26-28, translating into a 27% CAGR in profit after tax (PAT) over the same period.
“We expect BSE to witness a strong recovery in volume growth, aided by rising member participation an improving P/N ratio. An improved growth trajectory in the cash segment, robust demand for co-location, and the strong positioning of the Star MF platform will also contribute to the company’s performance,” the brokerage said in a note.
The brokerage raised its revenue estimates by 8%/10% and PAT estimates by 10%/12% for FY27/FY28, respectively, factoring in the strong volume run-rate, the potential benefit from the CAS reversal and higher cash market volumes following NSE’s listing. A sustained recovery in volumes and further improvement in the premium-to-notional ratio could provide additional support.

 AI Summary
 Silver prices have fallen more than 50% from their peak ahead of Dhanteras. Should investors buy now or wait for prices to fall further? Here's what market experts Ajay Kedia and Manav Modi of Motilal Oswal Financial Services say.
 + Follow on Google Add as preferred source 
 Silver prices have crashed more than 50% from their peak ahead of Dhanteras, leaving investors wondering whether to buy now or wait for a further correction. Ajay Kedia, director of Kedia Advisory, sees the sharp fall as an opportunity to accumulate silver gradually. However, Manav Modi, commodities analyst at Motilal Oswal Financial Services, cautions that prices could fall further. Here is what the two market experts say about silver's outlook and whether investors should buy now or wait.
MCX silver futures for December were trading at ₹1,93,413 per kg at 7:30 pm on October 26.
According to Kedia, silver has experienced extreme volatility in 2026. MCX silver plunged 54.10% from its January peak of ₹4,20,048 per kg to ₹1,92,800 per kg on October 23, 2026. International silver prices corrected 56.04% from $121.64 to $53.47.
Kedia attributed the reversal in silver's traditional safe-haven appeal to the US-Iran conflict and rising inflation risks. With Brent crude trading above $110, he said concerns about inflation had increased expectations of US Federal Reserve rate hikes, putting pressure on bullion prices.
He also pointed to weakness in equity markets and a 37% decline in UAE property transaction volumes during early March as signs of broader investor caution and liquidity pressures.
Kedia believes the correction could offer investors an opportunity to accumulate silver gradually.
Responding to whether investors should buy silver after the sharp fall, Kedia said they could consider doing so, describing a 50% decline as rare.
He said silver's structural fundamentals remain supportive, with nearly 50% of demand linked to industrial applications and persistent supply deficits.
Kedia identified $50 as a crucial support level for international silver prices. He added that the metal could potentially recover towards $90–$100 by next Dhanteras as geopolitical pressures ease, although volatility may persist.
Manav Modi of Motilal Oswal Financial Services expects silver to remain volatile over the next six to 12 months. He said its direction would depend largely on US interest-rate expectations, the dollar and industrial demand.
“Silver could hover around $50-$65 range any break either side could decide further direction of the metal,” Modi said.
The outlook suggests that silver's next move will depend on whether prices remain within this range or break decisively above or below it.
Modi said the correction has improved entry levels but warned that prices could fall further. He advised new investors against committing their entire investment amount at once.
Instead, he recommended staggered purchases to reduce the risk of investing the full amount just before another decline.
Modi also advised investors to keep silver as a measured part of a diversified portfolio, taking into account their investment horizon and risk appetite. He cautioned against using leverage to invest in the metal.
Investors should also consider the differences between physical silver, exchange-traded funds (ETFs) and other investment platforms, as costs, liquidity and tracking can vary.
 Key factors that could drive silver prices 
The outlook for silver will depend on several factors over the coming months.

 Symbiotec Pharmalab shares gained after Motilal Oswal initiated coverage with a buy rating and a target price of 1,430 rupees, citing the company's evolution into an integrated API, CDMO, and complex injectables platform. ICICI Direct also holds a buy rating with a 1,540 rupees target.
 + Follow on Google Add as preferred source 
 Shares of Symbiotec Pharmalab Ltd. gained on Monday, October 26, after brokerage firm Motilal Oswal initiated coverage on the stock indicating an upside of 23%.
The brokerage has initiated a "buy" rating with a target price of ₹1,430 per share.
Motilal Oswal said Symbiotec Pharmalab has evolved from a steroidal active pharmaceutical ingredient (API) manufacturer into an integrated platform spanning API fermentation-led CDMO, and complex injectables, backed by manufacturing investments and backward integration.
It said the company is a leading corticosteroid/hormone API supplier, with a total addressable market (TAM) of $800 million, and is expanding into fermentation-based and high-value complex APIs having TAM of $92 billion and 10.4% compound annual growth rate (CAGR) over the calendar years 2024-2029.
Motilal Oswal said the company is already on a path to provide chemistry and fermentation-based capabilities and capacities as a CDMO platform in precision fermentation, industrial biotechnology and biologics, targeting a TAM of $50 billion. It has invested in building a manufacturing facility to forward integrate into double chamber vials, which not only enables better profitability but also enhances traction in the most heavily regulated market (the US).
Its long-standing customer relationships, regulatory capabilities and contracted business support growth visibility, commercialization of new capacities and higher utilization remain the key execution drivers, the brokerage said.
Symbiotec Pharmalab posted a revenue, EBITDA, PAT CAGR of 15%, 51% and 69% reaching ₹870 crore, ₹240 crore and ₹110 crore, respectively, over FY23-26, Motilal Oswal said.
Motilal Oswal expects the company's revenue to grow at a 33% CAGR to ₹2,030 crore, EBITDA to also grow at a 33% CAGR to ₹560 crore, and PAT to grow to ₹300 crore over financial year 2026-2029, led by new product launches, scale up of CDMO & injectable operations, and operating leverage.
It values the stock at 35 times its 12-month forward earnings to arrive at its target price, factoring in the company's established API base and earnings potential from the newer businesses.
 In a bull-case scenario, Motilal Oswal has a target price of ₹1,690 per share on the stock, an upside of 45%.
It assumes a 12-month forward earnings per share (EPS) of ₹44.5 and assigns a 38x price-to-earnings multiple.
The bull case factors in faster earnings growth, driven by accelerated commercialization of new API and fermentation capacities, stronger traction in CDMO contracts, faster scale-up of complex injectables and improved operating leverage. 
 In a bear-case scenario, the brokerage has a target price of ₹1,000 per share.
It assumes a 12-month forward EPS of ₹32.5 and assigns a lower 31x price-to-earnings multiple.
The bear case factors in delayed commercialization of new capacities, slower ramp-up of CDMO and complex injectables, weaker-than-expected API growth, and higher operating costs affecting profitability. 
 Motilal Oswal lists the following as key risks for the stock: 
Apart of Motilal Oswal, ICICI Direct is the only other analyst that has coverage on the stock, with a "buy" rating and target price of ₹1,540 per share, indicating an upside 32.3% from its previous closing price.
Shares of Symbiotec Pharmalab gained 7.4% to hit an intraday high of ₹1,250.1 apiece on Monday. The stock is currently trading 4.6% higher at ₹1,218.1. The stocks is up 23% from its issue price of ₹988.

Buy DCB Bank; target of Rs 312: Anand Rathi
 DCBBANK 
 Anand Rathi's research report on DCB Bank 
 DCB Bank reported a strong performance in Q2FY27, with RoA/RoE coming in at 1%/13.8%, ahead of our estimates. CASA ratio improved by 65bps q/q, while advances grew by a healthy 21.1% y/y, led by Gold, Corporate and Agri portfolios. Looking ahead, the management targets ~18-20% business growth in FY27e. Asset quality remained broadly stable, with net slippages coming in at 7bps. Outpacing credit growth, core operating profit grew by 26.2% y/y, as strong fee income and lowerthan-expected opex growth offset NIM compression. We expect the bank’s margin to recover and fee momentum to sustain, supporting a gradual improvement in profitability, going forward. Alongside moderate credit cost, these factors should drive RoE from 13.5% in Q2FY27 to >15% over the medium-term. 
 Outlook 
 We maintain BUY rating on DCB Bank with a 12-month TP of Rs312, valuing the stock at 1.1x FY29e P/ABV.
